meta.review: Ainize UX critique 3 — derivative publishing, composition, the daily bake

summary:
Ainize is a peer-to-peer marketplace for "knowledge": small trained memory-table patches (.npz) that anyone can load into a running LLM, live-test, publish and be paid for. Two earlier reviews covered the visitor's web (items 1–100) and the terminal, the node operator and the publisher (101–169). This one is about the three flows the owner named as the point of the product: take someone's knowledge, put my own data on top of it and publish it again; use several knowledges together; and bake fresh knowledge every day from live data and share it. I worked at commit 1037244 against the demo cluster (node-a :3402, node-b :3403, node-c :3404), the dataset-teach node (:3422), and throwaway nodes and private three-node clusters on a local ledger for anything that publishes, applies, subscribes or pays. Eight walks — the derivative creator obtaining a base and building on it, the composer as a visitor and as a developer, the daily publisher and the daily consumer, the money along the tree, and discovery — were run end to end, then every finding was re-checked against the code by an adversarial pass; what survived is below. Captures are in packages/e2e/results/ux3/. The lineage-first redesign in docs/lineage-teach-design.md exists and was read as the intended direction; the product is measured against it throughout.

**What the three flows are supposed to feel like.** Building on someone's knowledge should feel like starting from their questions: you see what X covers and what people asked it that it got wrong, you add your rows, the trainer puts yours on top of theirs, the result says "built on X · adds 12 questions · X still answers 10/10", and when it sells, X's creator is paid by a rule you both saw before you signed. Composing should feel like a stack you can see: three knowledges in an order you chose, a warning that says which questions the top one overrides, a console that lists what is in the model right now, and an unload that puts back what was underneath. The daily bake should feel like a channel: a cron line that trains, verifies, publishes and retires yesterday with real exit codes, and on the other side a subscription that quietly delivers this morning's version, says "as of 2026-09-04", refuses a day that failed verification, and lets you go back to yesterday.

**How far the running product is from that.** The primitives exist and several are excellent: the purchase receipt, the settle record with its per-address split, the supersede mechanism and Explore's "current only" filter, the watchdog that notices a reverted table within 20 s, the agent's transparent payment loop, `teach dataset get` for your own rows, and a CLI whose read commands emit complete JSON. But none of the three flows can be completed as described by the person it is for. A creator with a file cannot name a base in the browser at all, and one who names it from the terminal has it silently dropped unless the base happens to be LISTED on that node at that moment; what is recorded as "built on" is trained on the bare model, verified alone, and un-loading it reverts the parent. A composer's unload writes the factory table over every other loaded knowledge that shares rows, two overlapping knowledges make the node rewrite the model every 20 s forever, and nothing anywhere lists what is loaded in what order. A daily publisher cannot publish from the terminal, gets exit 0 on a failed bake, and finds that the verifier which subscribed to yesterday fails today; a daily consumer who subscribes receives nothing after that moment, loads rejected and retired bakes, and has no date to read. The money is real and the split is verifiable — but the share is whatever the derivative's seller configured, and it halves on day two of any chain.

**The three biggest gaps.**

**1. "Built on" is a label, not a relation.** Nothing in the pipeline honours the base. The dataset door hard-codes `patch_ids: []`; the chat door's one checkbox makes every loaded knowledge a parent; the CLI cannot separate comparison from base; and `createLessonDraft` keeps a parent only if it is LISTED at that instant, dropping the rest without a word — on node-u that is every lesson, including one the visitor named "derived from KRX codes lesson". The trainer sees at most eight parent samples as contrast and exports `before` = bare model; CHECKING applies the parents on top of the lesson (the reverse of deployment); the verifier scores the child alone, so a row permutation of A passed 2/2 as A's grandchild and as a merge; the child's own Origins tab lists its parent under "overlapping entries need reconciling". The licence is free text with no compatibility rule (CC-BY-SA → Proprietary → CC0 in two commands), the sheet promises 70 % where the arithmetic pays 49 %, and any node can declare any knowledge as its parent without holding it, with no notice to the author. The design doc says "if this is not shipped, nothing may be called built on" — and it is not shipped.

**2. The runtime does not know what is stacked on it.** Apply writes `after`, remove writes `before`, and the `applied` table has no order. So unloading one knowledge reverts every other loaded knowledge on the shared rows (a rollback to yesterday's bake wipes yesterday's too); two loaded versions of the same subject make the watchdog re-apply the loser on top of the winner every 20 s, indefinitely, holding the GPU lock while operator commands time out as "cannot reach node" and then execute anyway; the live test decides what is "already loaded" by sampling the table rather than asking the node, so a visitor's free test of a held-but-unloaded version rewrites the operator's pinned set; the agent bypasses the lock entirely and unloads by default; subscribe stacks older versions on top of pins and unsubscribe removes them underneath. No screen or command lists the loaded set in order — `status --json` reports `applied: []` with two loaded, the console shows a yes/no per purchase and nothing for subscription-applied items, and the overlap alert says only "2,170 memory entries — Pixelplus wins".

**3. A track is a snapshot, not a channel.** Subscribe buys and applies whatever is in the track at that second and never looks again — while the OpenAPI, README and dashboard say "keep it loaded", "apply + watchdog", "fetch every item … switch tracks automatically". It applies a bake that FAILED verification when the node already holds the body (every verifier does), buys every retired version the track ever carried, and reports one green tick for a partial failure. The publisher's side is no better: the dataset door has no `teach publish`, `teach train --wait` exits 0 on FAILED with `checks passed` over `taught 0/18`, an identical re-bake retires the real newer version, the verifier that subscribed to yesterday fails today and leaves it VERIFYING forever with `patch challenge` a no-op, and the operator can `announce` a failed lesson draft onto the ledger without the data provider's consent. There is no "as of" date anywhere; the day lives in the name string.

Below: 100 problems worth fixing, numbered 170–269, grouped by flow and theme and ranked within each; the table that follows lists the twenty that would change these flows most, across flows.

flows.name: A. Derivative publishing
flows.description: Take someone else's knowledge, add my own data on top, publish the result — and be credited and paid along the tree.

items.title: A creator's own node peered to the seller never sees the seller's knowledge, and nothing says why
items.surface: `ainize init --peer http://localhost:3402` → `peers`, `nodes`, `patch ls`, `patch buy`, `use` on the creator's node
items.problem: `ainize init --peer http://localhost:3402` defaults to `--ledger local`. The node then reports `peers 3`, `nodes` lists node-a/b/c with LEDGER `ain` and 0 failures — and `patch ls` prints `no patches match`, `patch buy krx-all-2761` and `ainize use krx-all-2761` print `error: patch not found`. packages/node/src/p2p.ts:86-97 syncs records only when `this.deps.ledger.kind === 'local'` ("record sync (local ledger only; AIN ledger reads the chain directly)"), and an AIN node serves `{"records":[],"cursor":0}` from `/p2p/records?since=0`. No command — init, peers add, status, nodes, patch ls — compares the peer's advertised ledger (`/p2p/info` says `ain`) with this node's, and `nodes` even shows BLOBS 0 for node-a, which holds four (api.ts:249-253 filters through `market.publicBlobs`, empty on a node with no catalogue).
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux3/derive-obtain-17-local-node-buy-from-ain.txt (status: peers 3, patches 0; `no patches match`; `error: patch not found` ×2); the `ainize nodes` table's LEDGER column reads ain for every peer and local for self; `curl :3402/p2p/records?since=0` → `{"records":[],"cursor":0}`; packages/node/src/p2p.ts:86-97.
items.user_cost: The first thing a derivative creator does — start my own node and point it at the marketplace — ends in an empty catalogue and 'patch not found' with every health indicator green. There is no way to obtain the base on your own node without guessing that the fix is `init --ledger ain --ain-provider …`.
items.fix: In `peers add` / `init --peer` (packages/cli/src/commands/init.ts, peers.ts) and in every p2p round (p2p.ts), compare `info.ledger` with `this.deps.ledger.kind`; when they differ, log and surface in `ainize status`, `ainize nodes` and `ainize peers ls` one line: `node-a publishes on the AIN ledger; this node reads the local record DAG, so its knowledge will never appear here — re-init with \`ainize init --force --ledger ain --ain-provider <url>\` or pass --node http://localhost:3402`. Make `patch get/buy/use <id>` on a not-found id ask known peers' `/api/patches/:id` and print `krx-all-2761 exists on node-a (AIN ledger) — this node cannot read that ledger` instead of the bare not-found.
items.theme: Obtaining a base
items.fixed_note: Every p2p round compares the peer's advertised ledger with this node's and logs the mismatch once; `/api/info.peer_status` and `/api/nodes.peer_status` carry {known, reachable, unreachable, verifiers, ledger_mismatch, mismatched[]}, and /api/nodes rows carry `reachable`, `ledger`, `ledger_mismatch` and `blobs_advertised` (the count that used to read 0 for a peer holding four). `ainize status` prints `peers N known · N answered · N verifiers`, `peers ls` and `nodes` mark the mismatched ledger, `peers add` and `init --peer` say it at the moment the peer is added, the Network page shows the same in EN and KO, and a 404 on GET /api/patches/:id names the peer that has the knowledge and why it can never appear here. Reproduced against a stand-in AIN peer. ADVERSARIAL RE-CHECK: reproduced live by starting an AIN-ledger node against the local-ledger cluster — /api/info.peer_status.mismatched names it, all three nodes logged the warning with the remedy, and `peers ls` shows the LEDGER column.

items.title: Teaching on top of a base this node does not hold uploads your dataset and then dies with `error: invalid: unknown knowledge krx-all-2761`
items.surface: `ainize teach train mine.csv --patch krx-all-2761` on node-u (:3422) and on any node that does not hold the base
items.problem: The CLI creates a teaching key, uploads the dataset, prints `2 of 2 lines will train`, and only then posts the job — which packages/node/src/teach.ts:559 rejects from `contextTargets` with `invalid: unknown knowledge ${id}` for any context id that is not in this node's catalogue or fails `mayUseEntry`. packages/cli/src/commands/teach-dataset.ts:312-314 builds `patch_ids` and posts with no `GET /api/patches/:id` pre-check, so the failure comes after the side effect, and the message names no remedy.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux3/derive-obtain-09-teach-on-unheld.txt (upload succeeds, `2 of 2 lines will train`, then `error: invalid: unknown knowledge krx-all-2761`, exit 1); packages/node/src/teach.ts:559; packages/cli/src/commands/teach-dataset.ts:312-314.
items.user_cost: The one command the help text offers for building on something ('knowledge id(s) loaded while teaching — the lesson then builds on them') fails after doing work, with an `invalid:` label that reads like an internal validation tag. The creator does not learn that the base must be held on the teaching node, nor (item 170) that this node cannot see krx at all.
items.fix: In `teachTrain` resolve every `--patch`/`--on` id via `GET /api/patches/:id` before uploading; on 404 print `krx-all-2761 is not on this node. To build on it the node must hold its file: \`ainize use krx-all-2761 --no-apply\` (25 AIN), or teach on a node that has it` and exit 2 without uploading. Server side, replace `invalid: unknown knowledge` with a structured `unknown_knowledge { id, hint: 'buy' | 'not_listed' }` and have the CLI render the hint.
items.theme: Obtaining a base
items.fixed_note: contextTargets now answers `unknown_knowledge` (typo or a knowledge this node has never seen — deliberately also what a stranger gets for a private draft) or `knowledge_not_held` (listed here, file missing), each with a hint the browser and the CLI render as a remedy; `teach train` resolves every --patch/--on id through the new GET /api/teach/bases/:id BEFORE uploading and exits 2 without the side effect. Node 473d2bc, CLI 69c17fa. ADVERSARIAL RE-CHECK: reproduced live — a typo’d id is refused before anything is uploaded with its own sentence and remedy. (The third case, a base held only for verification, was still open and is closed in 6955ba1 under item 327.)

items.title: What you receive for 25 is 270,053 rows of float32 with no questions — no surface says the training set is unavailable, none offers to copy a public one, and the 'portable recipe' is three hyperparameters and a path on the seller's disk
items.surface: `ainize patch buy krx-all-2761` → `data/blobs/<sha>.npz`; the knowledge page Overview (Training notes / Recipe block); `patch get`; teach-origin pages on node-u
items.problem: After `patch buy` the only artefact is the .npz (members addrs int64, before/after 270053×160 float32). The anchor carries 26 of the claimed 2,761 questions; `GET /api/patches/:id` has `dataset: null`, `license: null`, and no `path`. The design's Training-set block (SC-10), `GET /api/patches/:id/dataset` (§12.3) and `ainize dataset get` (§13) do not exist (`ainize dataset get krx-all-2761` → `Unknown arguments`). Two regimes share one page: node-u's `taught-my-rows-5f7f54` has rows 3 = queries 3 = samples 3, `license: CC-BY-4.0` and a `dataset {sha256, rows, source}` fingerprint block (PatchPage.tsx:281) — its whole training set is readable — while krx has 26/2,761, no licence, no dataset, and the same 'Sample questions (n)' list; neither says "you can/cannot build on the full set". For the readable ones the only way to build on them is to retype the rows: the dataset fork endpoint (api.ts:590 `/api/teach/datasets/:id/fork`) only forks the caller's own datasets and `ainize patch fork` is not a command. Meanwhile the Overview says "For other models it can be rebuilt from the recipe below" (detail.ts:105/129) over a recipe that is `corpus_template` + three hyperparameters (PatchPage.tsx:331-334), and the description ends `Source: results/train-all/rows-pin.npz (2026-08-30)` — a file only node-a's operator has.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux3/derive-obtain-08-received.txt (numpy members/shapes; `grep -c path` → 0); derive-obtain-02-overview-en-1280.png (recipe block, 'Sample questions (26) … 14 more'); derive-obtain-01-patch-get.txt; `ainize --node http://localhost:3422 patch get taught-my-rows-5f7f54 --json` (rows 3 / samples 3 / CC-BY-4.0 / dataset object) vs the krx JSON (samples 26, dataset null); `ainize patch fork krx-all-2761` → `Unknown arguments`; docs/lineage-teach-design.md §12.3, §13, SC-10, F10.
items.user_cost: A creator pays, opens the file, and finds bf16-style vectors — no way to see which of the 2,761 companies are covered, which wording was trained, or what to add; they learn that no training set exists only after paying. On the lessons that are fully public, the product makes them copy-paste questions by hand. A creator who takes the 'portable recipe' copy at face value chases a path that does not exist on their machine.
items.fix: Ship §12.3 (`GET /api/patches/:id/dataset` with `access`, `rows`, `preview`) and `ainize dataset get <id> [-o]`. Until then: render one SC-10 line per anchor on the page and in `patch get` — `Training set: 3 questions · public · CC-BY-4.0` / `Training set: 26 of 2,761 questions published · not provided by the creator — you cannot build on the full set` — and repeat it in the Buy tab above the price. For anchors whose samples equal their rows add `Copy into my datasets` (a teach dataset from `benchmark.samples` under the caller's key, `parent_patch` set) and `Download .jsonl`, exposed as `ainize patch fork <id>`. Add `path` to `GET /api/patches/:id` when `has_body` and print it in `patch get`. Label the recipe block 'Training notes (from the creator)' and only claim 'rebuildable' when `anchor.dataset.sha256` resolves to a blob; strip local disk paths from seeded descriptions (packages/node/src/seed.ts).
items.theme: Obtaining a base
items.fixed_note: The anchor carries its dataset (sha256, rows, access, licence) and the training set is a served blob; `ainize dataset get` and `patch fork` copy it (138a103, a6c324c, 3c523ef).

items.title: `patch get` says 'body on this node: yes' before you have bought it, and `patch buy` then charges for a download it reports as 'already present'
items.surface: `ainize patch get` / `patch buy` on a node that holds the file because it verified it (lab node-c; every verifier)
items.problem: packages/cli/src/commands/patch.ts:59-68 prints `body on this node  yes` from `has_body` regardless of purchase, and the only purchase indicator is a ` purchased` suffix on line 1 when true — `purchased: false` exists only in `--json`. `patch buy` then charges the full price and its own timeline prints `download  body already present; sha256 matches on-ledger anchor`. api.ts:882 documents that verifiers and authors are exempt from the download gate, but nothing on the buyer side distinguishes 'held for verification' from 'bought'. (The same rule lets a verifier subscribe to a whole track for free — item 259.)
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux3/derive-obtain-07-cli-buy.txt (pre-buy `body on this node yes`; post-buy `+77ms download body already present` after a 25 CREDIT charge; `--json` purchased/has_body/owned); money-trust-06-buy-chain.txt (four purchases, every one `body already present`); packages/node/src/api.ts:876-882.
items.user_cost: A creator on a verifier node either builds on a file they are not licensed to use (the text says the body is here) or pays for bytes they already have without being told; either way the purchase output is a surprise.
items.fix: In `patch get` print `purchased  no · file held because this node verified it (not licensed for use/teaching)` / `purchased  yes (tx …)` / `owned  yes`. In `patch buy`, when `has_body && !purchased`, print `you already hold the file (verifier copy); buying records the licence and pays the seller 25 CREDIT — continue? [y/N]` (honouring `--yes`).
items.theme: Obtaining a base
items.fixed_note: `patch get` prints a `licence` line before `body on this node`: 'yours — you published it' / 'bought by this node · tx …' (the tx read from /api/me/purchases) / 'NOT bought — the file is here because this node verified it, and verifying is not a licence to use, teach on or subscribe with'. `patch buy` says the same before the money moves and asks 'Pay … to license <id> (the file is already here)?'. Verified live on node-b, a verifier holding another node's body.

items.title: After buying, the web dead-ends at 'The file is stored on this node' with 'Buy again' as the only button
items.surface: Knowledge page › Buy tab after purchase (lab node-c web)
items.problem: The purchased state renders `Already purchased. The file is stored on this node.` (detail.ts:213) followed by the same primary Button now labelled `Buy again` (PatchPage.tsx:519-531, detail.ts:219) and the note 'Pays from this node's credit balance…'. No path, sha, download, 'Teach on top of this', 'Live test with it loaded' or 'Load into model' control — the 'Load into model' text below is a glossary note. The CLI prints the path exactly once, at purchase.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux3/derive-obtain-13-buy-operator-purchased-en-1280.png / -ko-360.png; derive-obtain-13 txt lines 56-60; packages/web/src/pages/PatchPage.tsx:519-531.
items.user_cost: The creator has just paid and has no next step toward building on it; the one affordance offered spends the money again.
items.fix: Replace the purchased block with the file sha + path (or `Download .npz` via `/p2p/blob/:sha?name=`) and three actions — `Live test with it loaded` (/chat/:id), `Teach on top of this` (/teach?on=:id, pre-selecting the base — item 176), `Load into model` — and demote `Buy again` to a text link `Buy another copy`.
items.theme: Obtaining a base
items.fixed_note: The purchased block now offers "Load into model", a link to the console and a collect path, with "Buy again" demoted to a text link behind a confirmation.

items.title: Publishing a derivative from your own node fails with `unknown parent patch` until you guess that the seller must be a peer; `patch import` drops the lineage with a warning
items.surface: `ainize publish … --parents <id>` / `patch publish --parents` / `patch import` on the publisher's own node
items.problem: `createDraft` requires every parent to be in this node's entry map — `if (!map.has(p)) throw badInput('unknown parent patch: …')` (packages/node/src/market.ts:313-314) — and a fresh node knows nothing; the error names no remedy. `patch import` (packages/cli/src/commands/patch.ts:374-378) catches the 404 and quietly publishes without the link ('imported without that lineage link'). `ainize publish --help` says only `--parents comma list of source knowledge ids (creators get a revenue share)`.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux3/derive-build-50-own-node-parents.txt: `publish … --parents pixel-base` → `error: unknown parent patch: pixel-base` (exit 1); after `peers add http://localhost:3712` + 10 s the same command succeeds with `parents : pixel-base (LISTED)`. packages/node/src/market.ts:313-314; packages/cli/src/commands/patch.ts:374-378.
items.user_cost: The publisher who trained on node A and sells from their own node B either gives up or publishes a root without credit — precisely the outcome the royalty system exists to prevent. (Distinct from item 170: this is the same-ledger case, fixable by peering.)
items.fix: When a parent id is unknown, resolve it: query configured peers' `/api/patches/:id` (and the AIN ledger on `ain` nodes) and cache the anchor before validating; if still unknown, error with `parent {id} is not known to this node — add the node that sells it (\`ainize peers add <url>\`) or pass --parent-url`. Make `patch import` refuse instead of dropping the link unless `--drop-lineage` is passed.
items.theme: Obtaining a base
items.fixed_note: `createDraft` resolves an unknown parent instead of refusing it: it re-reads the ledger, then asks the peers this node already talks to for that id's records and ingests them (signature-checked like any other gossip). Only then is it an error — `unknown_parent`, naming which peers were asked, `ainize peers add <url>` as the remedy, and what publishing without the link would cost. `patch import` refuses to drop a lineage link instead of warning past it; `--drop-lineage` is the explicit way to import a root anyway.

items.title: 'Loaded' and 'built on' are one thing: the dataset door cannot name a base at all, the chat door's one checkbox makes every loaded knowledge a parent, and the CLI flag cannot separate comparison from base
items.surface: Dataset door /teach/dataset/:id/settings (node-u); chat door LessonBasket checkbox; `ainize teach train --patch`
items.problem: TeachSettingsPage.tsx:99 hard-codes `patch_ids: [], builds_on_context: false` — there is no picker, no 'Start from' block, no mention of a base in the five steps — while its own step-3 copy (i18n teach.ts:456) promises the side-effect check asks 'plus the questions the knowledge you loaded answers', something the page offers no control for. In the chat door the only lineage control is one checkbox 'This builds on the knowledge I have loaded (its creators share in sales)' (LessonBasket.tsx:110-113, default false at ChatPage.tsx:376); `createJob` records `context` = every selected id and `builds_on` for all of them (teach.ts:742), so with pixel-base and pixel-sa loaded and the box ticked, the draft got both as parents. The CLI `--patch` forces `builds_on_context: patchIds.length > 0` (teach-dataset.ts:314), so loading a knowledge for comparison only is impossible from the terminal. Design SC-1/SC-4 ('Built on' row, 'Start from' block, `base_ids` vs `context_ids`) are absent.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux3/derive-build-31-nodeu-settings-no-base-{en,ko}-{1280,360}.png and .txt (full step-3 text, no base control); derive-obtain-16-upload-settings-en-1280.png; derive-build-41-chat-basket-ticked-en-1280.png (two loaded, one checkbox); derive-build-44-chat-job-status.txt ('taught with pixel-base, pixel-sa (builds on them)' → `parents : pixel-base (LISTED), pixel-sa (LISTED)`); derive-build-34-cli-train-two-parents.txt; packages/web/src/pages/TeachSettingsPage.tsx:96-104; packages/web/src/components/chat/LessonBasket.tsx:110-113; packages/node/src/teach.ts:742; packages/cli/src/commands/teach-dataset.ts:312-314.
items.user_cost: The owner's headline flow ('take someone's knowledge, add my data, publish') is impossible in the browser with a file: the publisher uploads rows, trains, publishes — an unrelated root with no credit to the base. In the chat door a creator comparing against two knowledges gives the 30 % pool to both, permanently, or — leaving the box off — credits nobody. There is no middle.
items.fix: Add the SC-4 block to TeachSettingsPage: a required radio `Start from: [Choose a knowledge…] / Start from scratch`, a picker limited to knowledge whose body is on this node, sending `base_ids: [base]`; re-run the dataset pre-flight with the base loaded (`POST /api/teach/preflight { base_ids, dataset_id }`) so 'already known' is judged against the base. In the chat basket replace the checkbox with the SC-1 base row (`Built on: {name} [Change]`, default: first loaded; `Also loaded, for comparison only: {others}`; the `teach.basket.base_consequences` line). API: split `patch_ids` into `base_ids` (≤ 1 for extend) and `context_ids`; CLI: `--on <id>` for the base, `--patch` stays comparison-only with a warning. Until the trainer actually loads base rows (item 178), copy must say 'checked against', not 'builds on'; drop the 'knowledge you loaded' clause from the dataset door's step 3.

items.fixed_note: TeachSettingsPage has the SC-4 "Start from" base picker sending base_ids; the chat basket has the base row (9254039) and the CLI has `teach train --on` distinct from --patch (a6c324c).

items.title: 'Builds on' is silently thrown away whenever the base is not LISTED at the moment the draft is created — on node-u that is every single time
items.surface: POST /api/teach/jobs → READY draft (both doors, `teach train --patch`), node-u and private clusters; the child's page
items.problem: teach.ts:1620-1621 `const parents = job.builds_on ? job.context.filter((p) => listed.has(p)) : []` keeps only bases that are LISTED right now and drops the rest without a message; `contextTargets` (teach.ts:555-565, market.ts:767-773 `mayUseEntry`) accepts any non-DRAFT entry as a base at job time, so REJECTED, SUPERSEDED, ANNOUNCED and never-verified knowledge are all accepted and later discarded. node-u has 136 knowledges, 0 peers and quorum 2, so nothing there is ever LISTED — every lesson taught 'on top of' something on node-u publishes as a root, and the lesson status keeps saying 'taught with X (builds on them)' after the parent was dropped. A visitor's lesson literally named 'derived from KRX codes lesson' is on node-u today with `parents: []`, `lineage {parents: [], children: []}` and a page that says 'none — original knowledge'.

items.user_cost: The publisher is promised (and the sheet repeats) that the original creators share in sales; the anchor goes on the permanent record with `parents: []`, the parent's author gets nothing, the child never appears under the parent, and nobody is told. The design makes this an explicit publish-time error; the product does the opposite.
items.fix: Validate the base at job creation (teach.ts `createJob`, after `contextTargets`): refuse REJECTED/CHALLENGED with `base_rejected`, redirect SUPERSEDED with `base_retired: {newer}`; for ANNOUNCED/DRAFT bases keep the ids on the job, record them as parents at `createLessonDraft` regardless of status, and block `publish()` with `409 parent_not_listed: {id}` ('Publish after {name} is listed'). Never filter parents silently; if a parent cannot be recorded, fail the request with the reason. CLI: print the refusal and exit 1; web basket/sheet: the design's `teach.basket.base_unlisted` / `teach.pub.base_unlisted` strings.
items.theme: Declaring the base and what gets recorded
items.fixed_note: A base is validated at job creation (base_rejected / parent_not_listed) and recorded from lineage.parents instead of being filtered by LISTED at draft time.

items.title: 'Built on' is only a royalty declaration: the child is trained on the bare model, checked in the reverse order, verified alone, and un-loading it rewrites the parent's overlapping rows back to the factory table
items.surface: Trainer (gradient backend), CHECKING, verifier, runtime apply/remove; the child's Origins tab
items.problem: teach.ts:1192-1199 (`parentSamples`) hands the trainer at most 8 parent benchmark samples as `contrast` (:1227); the trainer loads the disk table and records `original[addr]` at first touch (qwen3.8/train/teach.py:318-329), so `before` is the bare model, never the parent. CHECKING applies the lesson first and the parents on top (teach.ts:1553-1563, 'stack re-applied on top of the lesson') — the reverse of how a buyer will load them — and on the stub backend logs 'parents 0/0'. The verifier benchmarks the child alone (packages/node/src/verifier.ts has no notion of parents). At runtime apply writes `after` and remove writes `before` (qwen3.8/scripts/patch.py:32-33; market.ts:696-720), so un-loading a child that shares addresses with its parent reverts those parent rows to base. The child's page nevertheless says 'Origins: pixel-base' while its Overlap check lists the same parent as 'Different subject — overlapping entries need reconciling' (item 226).
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux3/derive-build-23-draft-lineage.txt (child shares rows with pixel-base/pixel-sa while declared built on pixel-base); derive-build-35 (node-a log 'READY: taught 6/6, locality 12/12, parents 0/0'); derive-build-39-child2-origins-en-1280.png; packages/node/src/teach.ts:1192-1199, :1227, :1553-1563; qwen3.8/train/teach.py:318-329; qwen3.8/scripts/patch.py:32-33; docs/lineage-teach-design.md F1, F2, F6, §1 goal 3 ('If this is not shipped, nothing may be called built on').
items.user_cost: The publisher believes they extended X; what they published is a stand-alone patch that may fight X on shared rows and that, when a buyer removes it, damages X in the buyer's model. The verified score says nothing about the combination.
items.fix: Until true on-top training (design §7, PR L3) ships: (1) stop labelling the relation 'built on' — call it 'credits {name}' on the basket, sheet, tree and CLI; (2) in CHECKING apply parents first, then the lesson, and record `parent_regression` in deployment order (design §7.6), failing with `teach.res.parent_broken`; (3) in the Overlap check exclude declared parents from 'need reconciling' and state 'shares {n} rows with its base — un-loading this knowledge restores the base model on those rows, not {parent}'; (4) in `market.removePatch`, after `runtime.remove`, re-apply applied entries whose address sets overlap (the same helper as item 208).
items.theme: Declaring the base and what gets recorded
items.fixed_note: A knowledge trained on top of others is verified with them underneath and scored per source; on-top registration, ordered apply/remove and the journal landed with it (f5055da, 49d8613).

items.title: 'Verified 2/2' on a derivative or merge verifies only the child's own publisher-chosen questions — a row permutation of A's file passed as a 'grandchild' and as a 'merge'
items.surface: Verifier (packages/node/src/verifier.ts); `ainize publish --parents`; the Verification tab of any child
items.problem: verifier.ts runs `anchor.benchmark.samples` of the child only (verifier.ts:49, 89, 103 — no reference to parents); `createDraft` accepts any existing id as a parent (market.ts:314). On a private cluster I published a row-permutation of the same fixture as a `--parents` child and it was LISTED 2/2 within a minute with `Grandchild: A <- B <- C` in its description; a 'merge' M of C and D passed the same way. Design §7.7/§9 (per-source, stratified verification) is absent from the tree.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux3/money-trust-03-nodea-publish-grandchild.txt, money-trust-04-bob-publish-merge.txt, money-trust-09-patch-get-lineage.txt (`pixel-deriv-c … verification 2/2 passed ✓ quorum`, attestations `free_generation=4/4 pre_apply=0/4`); packages/node/src/verifier.ts:49-103; packages/node/src/market.ts:314.
items.user_cost: A buyer reads 'Verified' on a child as 'verified as an addition to its base'; it is verified as nothing of the kind. Any file can be sold as a derivative of any knowledge with a full-marks tick.
items.fix: Implement design §7.7: `verifyStack` applies the declared bases then the child and scores `per_source` — the child's own samples, and a sample of each parent's — writing `{source, hit, total}` into the attestation; the page's Verification tab shows 'its own 4/4 · still answers pixel-base 8/8'. Until then, label the tick on any anchor with `parents.length > 0` as 'Verified alone (not as an add-on)'.
items.theme: Declaring the base and what gets recorded
items.fixed_note: The verification tab labels a derivative whose run carried no `per_source` as measured on its own questions only, not as an addition to its base; the per-source scoring itself was already recorded and logged by verifier.ts.

items.title: Rows that overlap the base's own questions are dropped silently: upload says '2 of 2 lines will train', the lesson trains 1, and no output names the dropped row or the reason
items.surface: `ainize teach train --patch <base>` and `teach status`; the web result page
items.problem: teach.ts:482-493 `overlapsListing` drops any fact whose prompt and answer match a benchmark sample of a LISTED/VERIFYING/ANNOUNCED knowledge, and :713-748 stores only counts (`preflight: {checked 2, of 2, known 0, overlaps 1}`). The CLI never renders per-row pre-flight (teach-dataset.ts has no rendering of `overlaps`/`already_known`), so `trained 1 of 2 questions` is the whole explanation; the web result says '1 more were left out because the same knowledge is already on sale on this node' without naming the row or the knowledge. The same status then reports `taught 0/2 trained sentences` against `1 of 2 questions` — two denominators for one lesson (CLI teach.ts:263 counts sentences). For someone extending X, overlapping X's own samples is the normal case — re-teaching a corrected answer — and the drop cannot be overridden.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux3/derive-obtain-10-teach-on-held.txt, derive-obtain-10-teach-status.txt (job JSON `preflight` object); derive-build-34-cli-train-two-parents.txt ('3 of 3 lines will train' → 'trained 2 of 3 questions'); derive-build-37-result-two-parents-en-1280.png; packages/node/src/teach.ts:482-493, :718-724, :748.
items.user_cost: A correction to the base's own question — the design's 'Correct it' path — is silently removed from the lesson; the publisher ships fewer facts than they think, cannot find which vanished without diffing files, and cannot tell which rows will survive before spending a GPU slot.
items.fix: Record dropped rows with `{index, reason: 'overlaps_listing' | 'already_known', listing_id}` on the job; print a per-row pre-flight table in `teach train` (line · question · will train / already answered by {base} / overlaps {listing} — dropped) mirroring the web PreflightList, and the same in `teach status`; count questions consistently (`trained 1 of 2 questions (1 dropped: overlaps krx-all-2761)`). Per design A1, a row that overlaps the declared base becomes `in_base` (counted, not dropped) or `base_conflict` (kept with confirmation, flagged 'changes {base}'s answer').
items.theme: Declaring the base and what gets recorded
items.fixed_note: Every dropped row is recorded with its index, prompt, reason (already_known / in_base / overlaps_listing), the answer that decided it and the knowledge that already teaches it; `teach status` prints them as a per-row table and the headline count is questions, in one unit, with the probe count on its own line.

items.title: When the base already answers your rows, the lesson FAILs with `already_known` but hides the answers it measured, exits 0, and may bounce QUEUED↔PREFLIGHT for minutes without a word
items.surface: `ainize teach train`/`teach status` after pre-flight; the PREFLIGHT loop
items.problem: The pre-flight asked the live model each question and got the base's answers (that is how it decided `already_known`), yet the FAILED table prints BEFORE `-` for every row: teach.ts:1049-1055 finishes FAILED without storing the measured answers on the facts. The command exits 0 on FAILED (teach-dataset.ts:350-361 returns any terminal status; bin.ts:57 sets exit 0). And on 'shared runtime busy' the job goes back to QUEUED with `blocked: 'lock'` and `waitForJob` prints status only — one run alternated QUEUED/PREFLIGHT four times over eight minutes (11:40:38 → 11:48:53) with no reason.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux3/derive-build-21-cli-train-on-unlisted-parent.txt (QUEUED/PREFLIGHT ×4, `error already_known: the model already answers all of this correctly`, BEFORE column `-`, `exit=0`); derive-build-22 first run; packages/node/src/teach.ts:1049-1055, :712-724; packages/cli/src/commands/teach-dataset.ts:350-361.
items.user_cost: 'Seeing what the base covers' is the first step of a derivative; the product knows the answers and throws them away, so the publisher re-asks each question by hand in chat, and scripts cannot detect the failure from the exit code.
items.fix: Keep `base_answer` on dropped rows (`preflight.dropped[]` on the job) and print them in the BEFORE column with status 'already correct — skipped'; make `--wait` exit non-zero on FAILED/NEEDS_MORE (item 239's exit-code table); when the worker re-queues because the runtime lock is held, log and print `waiting for the shared model (held by {label}) …` instead of flipping status.
items.theme: Declaring the base and what gets recorded
items.fixed_note: The pre-flight's measured answer travels on each dropped row and is printed in the ANSWER ALREADY THERE column; a busy shared model is now a named wait with a deadline instead of a silent QUEUED↔PREFLIGHT bounce (item 244), and the non-zero exit on FAILED/NEEDS_MORE was already in place from item 239.

items.theme: Declaring the base and what gets recorded
items.fixed_note: The Built-on block prints a warning line for every base with no measured parent_check — 'Not checked against X on this node', or that the node simulates its checks — and `teach status` prints the parents line whenever a lesson has a base instead of only when total > 0.

items.title: Anyone can declare your knowledge as their parent — no holding, no consent, no proof, and you are never told
items.surface: `ainize publish … --parents <id>` from a stranger's node; parent author's node log/events/dashboard
items.problem: `createDraft` (market.ts:312-314) requires only `map.has(p)`: no purchase, licence, holder or author check. `noticeOwnEvents` (market.ts:241-259) skips an entry unless it has an open challenge, a `superseded_by`, or a failed attestation — a new child anchor naming my id triggers nothing; there is no `lineage` event kind (market.ts log kinds: blob/branch/buy/patch/publish/runtime/settings/trade/usage/verify). I published a `--parents` child on my cluster and the parent's node logged only 'received 1 record(s) via push'.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux3/derive-obtain-14-publish-with-parents.txt (`✓ draft created: my-krx-addon` with parents krx-all-2761, no prompt); derive-build-51-parent-sees-stranger-child.txt (own-node child → only p2p/verifier lines); money-trust-19-bob-x-on-day1.txt; packages/node/src/market.ts:312-314, :241-259.
items.user_cost: A base creator has no way to say yes or no, and cannot spot a child that mislabels or mis-licenses their work (item 185) because they are never notified. Money and rights are attached to a declaration nobody checked.
items.fix: At publish with `--parents`, require the caller to hold the parent (purchased or authored) and apply the §6.4 licence rule (item 185). On ingest of an anchor whose `parents` include a local anchor, emit a `lineage` event (`{child} by {author} was published built on {parent}`) to the operator log, the parent's manage page and the notifications setting ('Everything — sales, verification results…'). Longer term, the design's `missing_dataset_parent` / `derivation` proof.
items.theme: Declaring the base and what gets recorded
items.fixed_note: `noticeLineageEvents` emits one `lineage` notice per child anchor naming a local one — who published it, at what price, whether that undercuts the base, and what share every sale of it pays — derived from the catalogue so it works on either ledger and by any route, written exactly once. No consent gate was added: the protocol has no way to refuse a declaration nobody needs your key to make, so the honest fix is that the base's creator hears about it immediately. Verified live: node-b published under node-a's base and node-a logged the warning.

items.title: A lesson that failed its checks shows 'PUBLISHED AS taught-on-krx-009fa7' while `patch get` on that id says 'patch not found'
items.surface: `ainize teach jobs` / `teach status` / `patch get <draft-id>` on lab node-a
items.problem: teach-dataset.ts:400 titles the column `PUBLISHED AS` and prints `j.patch_id ?? c.dim(j.draft_id)`, so a NEEDS_MORE lesson's private draft id appears under 'published'. `patch get` on that id then answers `patch not found` — api.ts:181 returns 404 for `e.status === 'DRAFT' && !isOperator(req)`, and the teaching-key holder is not an operator, so their own draft is unreadable via `patch get`.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux3/derive-obtain-18-lab-lineage.txt (`patch get taught-on-krx-009fa7` → not found; `teach status` 'private draft'); `teach jobs` column PUBLISHED AS; packages/cli/src/commands/teach-dataset.ts:400; packages/node/src/api.ts:181.
items.user_cost: The creator cannot tell whether their derivative exists, is public, or is private; the id the CLI gives them is not resolvable with the CLI.
items.fix: Rename the column to `KNOWLEDGE` with a `(private)` / `(listed)` suffix from `publish_status`; in api.ts:181 let the job's teaching key (signed v2 header) read its own DRAFT, and have `patch get` print `private draft — only you can see it; publish with \`ainize teach publish <job>\`` (item 238).
items.theme: Declaring the base and what gets recorded
items.fixed_note: The column is KNOWLEDGE, not PUBLISHED AS, and says which kind of id it is — (listed), (verifying), (private), (private · sent for review), (private · the operator declined it) — with one line under the table saying a private draft is not on the record and `patch get` cannot see it, naming `teach status` and `teach publish` instead. Both the `teach jobs` table and the node view in `teach status` use it. Verified live on a node whose lesson ended READY-unchecked with a private draft.

items.title: Any licence can be put on a derivative: a CC-BY-SA root became a Proprietary child and a CC0 grandchild without a word, and the consent text never mentions the parent's terms
items.surface: PublishSheet licence select (both doors); `ainize publish --parents … --license`; `teach.publish`; `market.createDraft`
items.problem: PublishSheet.tsx:17,36,113 offers all five licences with CC-BY-4.0 as default and never shows the parent's licence (grep parent → none); teach.ts:1742 writes `license: body.license ?? 'CC-BY-4.0'`; `createDraft` (market.ts:305-326) stores `license: input.license` as a free string and checks parents only for existence. There is no `licenseForChild`, `license_incompatible` or forced-licence line anywhere in core or node. Reproduced twice: a lesson with parents pixel-base (CC-BY-4.0) and pixel-sa (CC-BY-SA-4.0) published as Proprietary → 'Announced'; from the CLI, `publish … --license CC-BY-SA-4.0` then `publish … --parents <that> --license CC0-1.0` → both '✓ announced', and a free CC0 copy of bob's Proprietary derivative shipped its rows for 0 with bob never told (item 183). The sheet's two consents talk about 'this information' and 'personal data' — nothing about having the right to build on and resell the parent; the Publish button is correctly gated on both boxes (PublishSheet.tsx:54-55) but the payload is hard-coded `consent: {permanent: true, rights: true}` (:66) and the node (teach.ts:1725) trusts it.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux3/derive-build-36-publish-proprietary.txt and derive-build-39 (child page License Proprietary, Origins pixel-sa); money-trust-20-free-child-of-proprietary.txt (`--parents pixel-deriv-b --license CC0-1.0 --price 0` → announced; parent `license: Proprietary`); money-trust-31-free-child-buy.txt; packages/web/src/components/chat/PublishSheet.tsx:36-66,112-113; packages/node/src/teach.ts:1725,1742; packages/node/src/market.ts:305-326; docs/lineage-teach-design.md §6.4, §6.5.
items.user_cost: The publisher unknowingly breaches the share-alike terms of the knowledge they built on and cannot fix it ('Published knowledge is fixed on the public record'); the base author has no recourse. The permanent record carries a rights declaration nobody actually made about the thing that matters.
items.fix: Implement design §6.4 in one place — core `licenseForChild(parentLicences, requested)`: CC-BY-SA parent → force CC-BY-SA and render `teach.pub.ds_license_forced` with the select disabled; Proprietary parent → allow but label; unknown → 400 `bad_license`; incompatible → 400 `license_incompatible {parent, parent_license}` from both `teach.publish` and `market.createDraft`/`patch publish --parents`. Show the parent's licence on the sheet, add a third consent line when parents exist ('I have read {parent}'s licence ({licence}) and my licence complies'), send the real checkbox state, and store `declaration: {source, license, parents_ack}` on the anchor. Append 'Built on {name} by {author}' to the description automatically.
items.theme: Licence, consent and the publish sheet
items.fixed_note: core/lineage.ts refuses an incompatible child licence (license_incompatible / bad_license) on both the teach publish and the draft path.

items.title: The publish sheet promises 'You receive 70 % of every sale'; a built-on lesson pays the teacher 49 % — and the sheet cannot tell whether you built on anything, shows no parent price, and defaults the price to 0
items.surface: PublishSheet (chat + dataset doors); `ainize publish`'s contributor line; the settle record; the teacher page
items.problem: PublishSheet.tsx:125 renders `teach.pub.split` (i18n teach.ts:155) from `policy.shares` only: 'You receive {contributor}% of every sale … If you ticked "builds on", the creators of that knowledge receive the network's creator share ({lineage}%) first.' It never reads the job's parents, so it hedges with 'if you ticked' on a job that did tick it and names no parent. The real split (catalog.ts:262-291 `royaltySplit`) takes the 30 % pool first and carves the contributor's 0.7 from the remainder: 0.7 × 0.7 = 49 % — a 2-credit sale paid 0.98, not 1.40; the CLI's only number is `Dana 50 % (of this node's share of each sale)` (patch.ts:168) when the true figure was 3.5 of 10. The price field initialises to '0' (PublishSheet.tsx:35) with no sight of the parent's price (pixel-base sells for 5) or of what the parent's creators receive at the typed price — a 0-price child yields a 0 pool, so the 'creators share in sales' promise is empty by default.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux3/derive-build-25-publish.txt and derive-build-36 sheet screenshots (en/ko, 1280/360): split sentence verbatim, price '0'; derive-build-38-buyer-use.txt (settle at 2 CREDIT → royalty {node-a: 1.02, visitor 0xB02C…: 0.98}; teacher page 'owed 0.98'); derive-build-27-child-overview.txt ('Data provider: Taught by a visitor (70%)'); money-trust-07-settle-records.txt (pixel-deriv-b at 10 → Dana 3.5); packages/web/src/components/chat/PublishSheet.tsx:27-40,106-108,125; packages/core/src/catalog.ts:262-291; packages/cli/src/commands/patch.ts:168.
items.user_cost: The one number the teacher is asked to accept before an irreversible publish is wrong by 21 points of the price; nothing says which knowledge takes the 30 % or that both loaded knowledges will be paid; publishers undercut the base by accident or give the derivative away while the record says the base is credited.
items.fix: Add `split_preview` to `GET /api/teach/jobs/:id/publish-challenge` (and to `patch get` for drafts): `royaltySplit` on a unit price with names. Render the design's SC-8 `teach.pub.money` — 'Every sale: 30 % to the creators of pixel-base, pixel-sa · 49 % to you · 21 % to node-a' — drop the 'if you ticked' clause when no parents are recorded, show 'Built on {name} · sells for {price}' above the price field with a live payout line under it, and default the price to the parent's price (or the node default) when parents exist. Print the same computed percentages in `ainize publish` before announcing and on the child page instead of the raw contributor share.
items.theme: Licence, consent and the publish sheet
items.fixed_note: The publish sheet prices the real split from royaltySplit’s own output (split_preview on the publish challenge), names the parents, and drops the "if you ticked" hedge. ADVERSARIAL RE-CHECK confirmed the preview is the settle function’s output and fixed the trap underneath it (7b16d04): royaltyPlan read the sold anchor from the catalogue map rather than from the entry handed in, so any caller passing an un-gossiped anchor — a draft, a fork — walked no lineage and paid the whole pool to the seller.

The seller's Manage page disables the free-text License field once published (ManagePage.tsx:253-263 `disabled={!isDraft}`, 'Published knowledge is fixed on the public record'), so the flagship can never acquire one.

(The publisher-side free-text field is critique-2 item 161; this is the buyer-facing placeholder and the post-publish lock.)

items.title: A derivative can only ever be a new root-style listing named `taught-<slug>-<hex>` on its own topic — no version, correction, fork or track choice exists, Explore grows one topic chip per lesson, and versions, forks and unrelated siblings all wear the same 'Newer version' chip
items.surface: Publish sheet fields; `createLessonDraft` id/schema; Explore Topic filter (136 chips on node-u); the Origins tab's tree
items.problem: `createLessonDraft` builds the id from the lesson name plus 3 random bytes and a unique benchmark schema `taught/<slug>-<hex>` (teach.ts:1604-1620; teach-recipe.ts:71-76) — by design F15 so the child never supersedes or relates to the parent's subject; the sheet offers only Name/Description/Price/Licence (PublishSheet.tsx:100-115). On node-a the supersede records (pixelplus-087600 → krx-all-2761, ep6 → krx, ep12 → krx) come from `reconcileSupersedes`'s 2,170-row overlap between a 1-fact and a 2,761-fact item, so a single fact wears 'Newer version: krx-all-2761' beside a genuine epoch chain that wears the same chip.

items.theme: Licence, consent and the publish sheet
items.fixed_note: `publish --kind extend|contradict|update|merge` records what a child IS to its bases, and the numbers under the claim are the node's: `measureDerivation` intersects the two address sets for added/changed rows, so a kind can only be declared on a base whose file is here, and `update` is refused on somebody else's knowledge. The family tree already renders edge kinds, so it reaches the page unchanged. Explore's subject filter collapses every `taught/<slug>-<hex>` into one chip (`?schema=taught/*`; a trailing `*` is a prefix on the catalogue filter) and caps the rest at 8 with "+n more". A child already inherits its parent's topic (item 189). NOT done, and deliberately: the child's benchmark SCHEMA is still not inherited — sharing a schema would let two sibling lessons supersede each other, which is what F15 avoids — and the publish sheet's outcome selector belongs to the teach-mode surface another workstream owns.

items.title: Publishing a child from the CLI records the parent as 'conflicting knowledge', drops the parent's topic, queues a supersede of its own base, and prints no royalty preview
items.surface: `ainize publish … --parents krx-all-2761` (lab node-c) and the child's page
items.problem: `ainize publish 픽셀플러스.npz --parents krx-all-2761 --price 3` printed `✓ draft created` and nothing about the split; `patch get my-krx-addon` then lists `krx-all-2761 2,170 shared rows yes → conflicting knowledge` in the overlap table while naming it as the parent one block above (`conflicts()` at market.ts:368-388 has no parent exclusion); the topic defaulted to `patches/qwen3-8-flash-next` (market.ts:322) instead of the parent's `finance/krx`, so the child is not 'other knowledge on this subject' from the base's page; and because the child shares the schema and overlaps, `announce()` records a `pending_supersede` of its own parent (market.ts:402, 430-446) — once verified it would retire krx-all-2761.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux3/derive-obtain-14-publish-with-parents.txt; derive-obtain-18-lab-lineage.txt; derive-obtain-19-child-lineage-en-1280.png ('Track main · topic patches/qwen3-8-flash-next'); packages/node/src/market.ts:312-322, :368-388, :402, :430-446.

items.fix: When `parents` is given: default `topic_path`/`branch` to the first parent's; in `conflicts()` skip pairs where one is the declared parent of the other (design §12.6, PR L0); never queue a supersede against a declared parent; record `parent_sha256` per parent; and have `publish` print `each sale of 3 CREDIT → 2.1 to you, 0.9 shared by the creators of krx-all-2761 (node-a)` before announcing (from `royaltySplit`).
items.theme: Licence, consent and the publish sheet
items.fixed_note: A child with no explicit --topic/--branch inherits its first parent's, so it lands as other knowledge on the base's subject. `conflicts()` marks a declared parent/child overlap `lineage`, `patch get` prints "yes → its base, not a rival" and `supersedable()` never queues one, so a child can no longer retire the knowledge it credits. GET /api/patches/:id carries `split` — what one sale pays and to whom, by name, from the same royaltyPlan that settles it — and `publish` prints it before the announce. Verified on a throwaway cluster: h-child inherited finance/hbase, the overlap reads as its base, and the ledger holds no supersede.

items.title: The creator share is whatever the derivative's seller configures — bob set `market.royaltyShare` to 0 and alice's 30 % became 0 while her page still says 30 %

items.problem: `royaltySplit(entry, map, price, this.cfg.market.royaltyShare)` takes the share from the selling node's own config.json, and the settle record (signed only by the seller) is accepted by every node as-is: `creditBalance` (market.ts:544) and payouts.ts:67 simply trust `settle.body.royalty`, no verifier recomputes the split, and the anchor has no share field (types.ts:82-115). items.fix: Make the share part of the anchor, not the node: at `createDraft` write `royalty_share` (a network minimum from a shared constant, or the max of every parent anchor's declared share) into the child anchor; `settlePayment` uses `entry.anchor.royalty_share`; verifiers/peers reject a settle record whose `royalty` map ≠ `royaltySplit(anchor, map, amount, anchor.royalty_share)` (log `settle_split_mismatch`, exclude from balances). Render the share on the lineage tab from the anchor.
items.theme: Money along the tree

items.title: A daily chain halves the base creator's share on day 2 and silently drops her to 0 on day 18 — and a data provider's share silently applies to every descendant's sale with no rule shown anywhere
items.surface: `royaltySplit` (packages/core/src/catalog.ts:233-291); every settle record along a chain
items.problem: The pool is split equally among unique ancestor authors including the seller's own older versions (whose slice folds back into the seller, catalog.ts:264-268), so the moment a baker lists yesterday's version as a parent — design §11 example 8 recommends exactly this — every outside creator's share is halved. The walk stops at `if (depth > 16) return;` (catalog.ts:245), so an ancestor 18 hops up is never visited: the original creator's royalty goes to zero with no message. Re-run on the shipped core/dist over a 20-day chain rooted at alice (share 0.3, price 10): day 1 {alice 3, baker 7}; days 2–17 {baker 8.5, alice 1.5}; days 18 and 20 {baker 10}. Pass 1b (catalog.ts:270-277) additionally carves each ancestor anchor's slice for that anchor's contributors, so Dana — told '50 %' on B — receives 3.5, 0.75 and 0.5 on three different sales (B, C, M) and the only copy anywhere is patch.ts:168's '(of this node's share of each sale)', which describes pass 2 only.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux3/money-trust-10-depth-cutoff.txt (the eight splits quoted above); money-trust-07-settle-records.txt (Dana 3.5 / 0.75 / 0.5); packages/core/src/catalog.ts:245, :264-277; docs/lineage-teach-design.md §11 (keeps the equal-split rule, F9).
items.user_cost: A base creator whose knowledge underpins a daily feed is paid half from day 2 and nothing from day 18, with every screen still saying 'the original creators automatically receive a share'. Data providers are paid amounts they cannot reconcile with the one percentage they were shown.
items.fix: Decide and document the chain rule in one place (docs/lineage-teach-design.md §11) and make the code match it: exclude same-author ancestors from the *count* when folding them back (so a version chain does not dilute outsiders), replace the depth-16 cut with a visited-set walk over the whole chain or an explicit `ancestors_truncated` flag that is rendered, and add the two-parent, 20-deep and provider-on-ancestor cases to packages/core/test/core.test.ts. Print the provider rule where the share is set (`data-provider share 50 % of this node's share — also of this node's lineage share from knowledge built on it`).
items.theme: Money along the tree
items.fixed_note: The lineage walk lost the depth-16 cut for a cycle-safe queue and no longer counts the seller's own ancestors as payees or divisors, so a 20-day chain still pays the base creator 3 of 10 on day 20; a provider credited on the seller's own earlier version is paid from the seller side instead, docs/lineage-teach-design.md §11 was rewritten to match and the two-parent, 20-deep and provider-on-ancestor cases are in core.test.ts.

items.title: Unloading one knowledge writes the base model over every other loaded knowledge that shares its rows — the console keeps saying 'In model: yes', and a rollback to yesterday's bake wipes yesterday's rows too
items.surface: `ainize patch remove <id>` / console Unload / `branch unsubscribe`; qwen3.8/scripts/patch.py remove; watchdog
items.problem: `removePatch` runs `patch.py remove`, which writes the removed file's `before` (= the bare model) to every address it owns (market.ts:710-721; qwen3.8/scripts/patch.py:30-33), never asking what else is loaded on those rows; `store.clearApplied` clears only the removed id (store.ts:81 `applied` has no position column, :510 unordered `SELECT * FROM applied`). The watchdog re-applies a neighbour only when a 2,000-row sample says it is 'closer to original than trained' (market.ts:723-741; patch.py:32-37 compares max-abs-diff), so a small overlap is effectively invisible to it and a large one is caught up to 20 s later, in a different order. Three faces of one defect: (a) node-b, three loaded, `patch remove pixelplus-087600` → 11:58:04 `WARN runtime: patch krx-all-2761-ep12 reverted (restart?) → re-applying`; (b) node-d, pinned final + pixelplus, remove pixelplus → the pinned final answered 픽셀플러스 → '368770' instead of 087600 for the whole 75 s watched, no watchdog line, `/api/runtime` still listing it; (c) the daily consumer's rollback: `✓ removed krx-daily-2026-09-02` → `patch.py status day1.npz` = `applied: no | diff to original 0.0000` while `/api/runtime` listed day-1 as applied. Design goal 4 / §8.4 (journal, `has_dependents`, re-assert) is not in the tree; `GET /api/runtime/stack` → 404 HTML.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux3/compose-visitor-b-10-buyer-flow.txt and compose-visitor-b-14-private-cluster.log (lines 129-137); compose-dev-16-overlap-agent-script.txt PART 1 (completion '087600, 참' → '368770 ' → still '368770 ' 75 s later; `node.log runtime lines since …: 2`); daily-consumer-21-manual-update-rollback.txt; daily-consumer-25 first block (`removed krx-daily-2026-09-02` then `krx-daily-2026-09-01 reverted (restart?) → re-applying`); packages/node/src/market.ts:710-741; packages/node/src/store.ts:81,510; qwen3.8/scripts/patch.py:30-37; docs/lineage-teach-design.md F4, F5, §8.
items.user_cost: A buyer who loads three overlapping knowledges and unloads one has 2,154–241,992 rows replaced by the base model for up to 20 s or forever; every live test, verification and customer on that node gets base-model answers while every screen says the knowledge is loaded. The rollback a daily consumer reaches for on a bad day leaves the model answering from nothing.
items.fix: Short term in `Market.removePatch` (market.ts:710): take the runtime lock once, write `before` for the removed patch, then re-apply every other row of `store.listApplied()` whose address set overlaps the removed body (core's npz reader already computes this for `conflicts`) in stored order before releasing; print `restored krx-all-2761 on 2,170 shared rows` in the CLI/API result; do the same after `runtime.verify` and in `unsubscribe`. Add `position INTEGER` to `applied` and make the watchdog re-assert the whole ordered set. Then ship the design's journal (`prev` from the hook, `has_dependents`, `GET /api/runtime/stack`). Change bin.ts:226's help from 'Restore original rows (un-apply)' to 'Unload from the model'.
items.theme: The runtime stack: apply, remove, watchdog
items.fixed_note: `applied` is an ordered stack with a per-layer journal; remove unwinds and re-asserts the layers above (49d8613) and `GET /api/runtime/stack` reports it (0d85627).

items.title: Two loaded knowledges that share rows make the watchdog fight itself every 20 s, forever — the older one is re-written on top of the newer one and the lock is busy for everyone
items.surface: `market.watchdog` (20-s tick) with two overlapping knowledges applied; every apply/remove/chat waiting on the lock
items.problem: The watchdog loops over the `applied` table one patch at a time, asks `patch.py status` per patch and re-applies whichever looks reverted (market.ts:723-741; server.ts:183 `setInterval(…, 20_000)`). With ep12 and the final loaded (241,992 shared rows, 100 % of ep12), whichever was written last makes the other look 'reverted', so each tick re-applies the loser on top of the winner. There is no notion of order or top-of-stack (design F5). On node-d `grep -c reverted node.log` = 70 at 11:35 (67 × ep12, 4 × the final), first 09:02:17, ticks 20 s apart, 76 by the 11:39 restart; it resumed 15 s after `branch subscribe` put ep6+ep12 on top.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux3/compose-dev-07-remove-overlap.txt (`ep12 reverted → re-applying` at 09:05:36, 09:06:16, 09:06:36, 09:07:17, then `krx-all-2761 reverted` 09:07:30); compose-dev-13-remove-semantics.txt (11:41:45, 11:42:25, 11:42:45); compose-dev-15-subscribe.txt; packages/node/src/market.ts:723-741; packages/node/src/server.ts:183.
items.user_cost: The effective answers on 241,992 rows flip between versions every tick; every re-apply is a ~3 s GPU write under the shared lock, so operator commands queue for minutes (item 212) and visitors' live tests wait behind a node doing nothing useful. The developer sees only WARN lines blaming a 'restart?'.
items.fix: Make the watchdog stack-aware: keep `position` in `applied` (store.ts:81), check only the topmost patch's rows for each address set (or simply `isApplied` of the last-applied patch), and on a detected revert re-apply the whole set in `position` order in one locked section instead of per patch. Refuse (`409 overlaps_loaded`) or at least warn on `apply` when the new body shares rows with an applied one, naming the loser: `krx-all-2761-ep12 will override 241,992 rows of krx-all-2761`. Reword the WARN: `{id} rows were overwritten ({last runtime op}) → re-applying`.
items.theme: The runtime stack: apply, remove, watchdog
items.fixed_note: The watchdog probes and rebuilds the whole ordered stack inside the runtime lock instead of re-applying one patch at a time.

items.title: '✓ removed krx-all-2761' was false: the watchdog re-applied it 114 ms later, leaving 270,053 rows of an 'unloaded' knowledge in the model with nothing in the database that knows it
items.surface: `ainize patch remove <id>` / console Unload on any node with the 20-s watchdog
items.problem: The watchdog iterates a `listApplied()` snapshot taken before the remove and calls `runtime.isApplied()` (runtime.ts:320-324, unlocked, a 2,000-row sampled `patch.py status`) while `removePatch` is mid-write; it reads a half-restored table, decides the patch 'reverted', and its `runtime.apply()` (market.ts:731-732) runs the instant the remove releases the lock — after `store.clearApplied` has run. The CLI had already printed the success line (patch.ts:216-219). Only a second `ainize patch remove` of a knowledge the node says is not loaded cleared it.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux3/compose-visitor-b-14-private-cluster.log lines 131-132: `11:57:03.394 INFO runtime: removed krx-all-2761: 뺌: 270053행 2.9s` then `11:57:03.508 WARN runtime: patch krx-all-2761 reverted (restart?) → re-applying`; `GET /api/runtime` → applied `[pixelplus-087600, krx-all-2761-ep12]`; compose-visitor-b-13-cleanup.txt (second remove → `POST /api/chat` reports `was_applied: False`); packages/node/src/market.ts:724-733; packages/node/src/runtime.ts:320-324.
items.user_cost: The buyer believes the knowledge is out of the model; every live test, verification and customer on that node keeps getting its answers, and the console/CLI/`/api/runtime` say `applied: []`. On a shared serving model it contaminates everyone else's 'Before loading' column.
items.fix: Run the watchdog body inside `runtime.exclusive('watchdog', …)` and re-read `store.listApplied()` after acquiring the lock, skipping any id not in the fresh list; never call `runtime.apply` for an id whose row was cleared. Cheaper still: a `removing: Set<string>` in Market that `removePatch` sets before the write and clears after, which the watchdog skips.
items.theme: The runtime stack: apply, remove, watchdog
items.fixed_note: The watchdog reads listApplied inside the lock, so it can no longer re-apply a patch whose row a concurrent remove has already cleared.

items.title: The live test decides what is 'already loaded' by sampling the table, not by asking the node: it reports leftovers as 'was already loaded', leaves them on the shared model, and a visitor's test of a held-but-unloaded version silently rewrites the operator's pinned set
items.surface: POST /api/chat compare mode (`chatInner`); the picker's contamination banner; the Before column
items.problem: `GET /api/chat/patches` returns `applied: market.pinnedPatchIds()` = `store.listApplied()` (api.ts:389, market.ts:922) — the banner knows only what this node pinned. But `chatInner` decides `wasApplied[i]` with the sampled heuristic `runtime.isApplied(t.path)` (market.ts:832; runtime.ts:320-324; patch.py:32-37 'closer to trained than to original') and in `finally` re-applies anything that `wasApplied` (market.ts:863-871), never re-asserting pinned patches outside the request. Two consequences. (a) When the shared table is dirty — another node's verification, a crashed test, item 210 — the visitor's bubble says '· was already loaded' with no banner, the Before column is patched, and the test re-asserts the leftover for everyone: on node-a with `applied []`, `POST /api/chat patch_ids=[krx-all-2761,pixelplus-087600]` → `pixelplus-087600 was_applied True`, and the identical greedy question (`temperature: 0`, runtime.ts:226) answered Before = `054410` then `087600` 90 s apart, `136950` later. (b) A same-lineage version reads as applied although never loaded: on node-d with `[krx-all-2761, pixelplus-087600]` pinned, an anonymous `POST /api/chat {patch_id: krx-all-2761-ep12}` returned `was_applied: True, applied_ms: 2835`, unloaded ep12 for the base column (writing disk base over 241,992 rows of the pinned final, base answer '361390'), then left ep12 loaded on top; `/api/runtime` unchanged.

items.title: An apply or remove that waits more than five minutes behind the lock comes back as 'cannot reach node … (fetch failed)', exit 2, and the node then executes it anyway
items.surface: `ainize patch apply|remove`, `ainize use` while the shared model lock is busy; packages/cli/src/client.ts
items.problem: `patchRemove`/`patchApply` pass `timeoutMs: 10 * 60_000`, but client.ts:19-28 wraps fetch with only `AbortSignal.timeout` and Node 20's undici gives up on response headers after its default 300 s; every fetch throw is mapped to `cannot reach node at … Is it running?` with exit code 2. The node keeps the request queued and runs it when the lock frees — my remove was answered 'fetch failed' at ~11:43 and executed at 11:48:08 (`removed krx-all-2761-ep12: 뺌: 241992행 4.5s`), with curl succeeding against the same node before and after.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux3/compose-dev-13-remove-semantics.txt (`error: cannot reach node at http://localhost:3536 (fetch failed). Is it running? …` `exit=2`; node.log `[11:48:08] INFO runtime: removed …`); packages/cli/src/client.ts:19-28.
items.user_cost: A script sees the 'node is down' exit code, takes the corrective branch (restart, retry, alert) while the node is healthy — and the remove it thought failed lands minutes later, un-teaching rows underneath whatever the script did next.
items.fix: Make apply/remove asynchronous: POST returns `202 { job, position_in_queue }` and the CLI polls `/api/runtime` (or `/api/runtime/jobs/:id`) printing `queued behind chat:… since 11:43 — Ctrl-C leaves it queued`. Until then, pass a custom undici `dispatcher` with `headersTimeout` = the request's `timeoutMs`, and map a headers-timeout to `still running on the node — check \`ainize logs --kind runtime\`` with a distinct exit code, never 2.
items.theme: The runtime stack: apply, remove, watchdog
items.fixed_note: POST /api/patches/:id/apply|remove accept {async:true} and answer 202 with a job the CLI polls (printing what holds the shared model), and a client-side timeout is no longer reported as `cannot reach node` with exit 2 but as "the node did not answer… it may still be running" with exit 4. ADVERSARIAL RE-CHECK: reproduced live — POST /api/patches/:id/apply {async:true} answers 202 with a job, and GET /api/runtime/jobs reports it failed with the real reason instead of "cannot reach node" followed by a silent execution.

items.title: The persistent order of the set is whatever SQLite rowid happens to be: re-applying a knowledge moves it to the end, and a serving restart replays the set per patch in that order
items.surface: `ainize patch apply <id>` repeated, `ainize use` on a held item; the `applied` table; watchdog after a vLLM restart
items.problem: `setApplied` is `INSERT OR REPLACE` (PRIMARY KEY patch_id → delete+insert → new rowid) and `listApplied` has no ORDER BY (store.ts:508-510), so `/api/runtime`'s order is insertion order and any re-`apply` — including `use`'s fast path that re-applies a held item (patch.ts:296) — rotates it; after a vLLM restart the watchdog re-applies each patch independently (market.ts:723-741), so 'last wins' after a restart may differ from what the developer set up. Survival of the set across a *node* restart works (praise).
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux3/compose-dev-07-remove-overlap.txt (after `patch apply krx-all-2761-ep12` the stored order became `[('krx-all-2761',…,'purchase'), ('krx-all-2761-ep12',…,'manual')]` — the older version on top); compose-dev-16 PART 3 (`use krx-all-2761` then `use pixelplus-087600` re-applied both and reordered); packages/node/src/store.ts:508-510; packages/cli/src/commands/patch.ts:296.
items.user_cost: A developer who established 'A below B' cannot rely on it after a `use A` refresh or a model restart; there is no way to state the order explicitly.
items.fix: Add `position INTEGER` to `applied` (design §5.4), keep it on re-apply, order `listApplied()` by it, accept `--position` / `--below <id>` on apply, and make the watchdog re-assert the whole stack in position order in one lock section (item 209).
items.theme: The runtime stack: apply, remove, watchdog
items.fixed_note: The `applied` table carries `position` (0 = bottom), `listApplied()` orders by it, `assertStack`/`applyStack` renumber the whole stack, re-applying a held knowledge answers “was already loaded” instead of rotating it, and the watchdog re-asserts the entire stack in position order in one lock section.

items.title: Subscribing loads a track's (older) versions on top of what the operator pinned, and unsubscribing removes them in the same order underneath it — with no overlap check, no warning, and the 'manual' vs 'subscription' reason rendered nowhere
items.surface: `ainize branch subscribe|unsubscribe`; POST /api/branches/:name/subscribe; the console track card
items.problem: `subscribe` buys and applies each track id in track order after whatever is already loaded (market.ts:961-978), so `finance/KRX-history` put ep6 then ep12 (241,992 shared rows each) on top of the pinned final; `unsubscribe` loops the same order calling `removePatch` (:979-981) — for ep6 then ep12 with identical address sets, removing ep6 first overwrites ep12's rows with base, the watchdog re-applies ep12 seconds later, then ep12 is removed, and the pinned final is reverted on 241,992 rows (item 208). The `reason` column exists in `applied` (store.ts:81) but the dashboard shows yes/no and `chat --list` prints ids only; the console card shows '2 knowledge · 0 subscriber(s)' with no names and no order (operator.ts:104).
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux3/compose-dev-15-subscribe.txt: before `[('krx-all-2761','manual')]`; after subscribe `[…, ('krx-all-2761-ep6','subscription:finance/KRX-history'), ('krx-all-2761-ep12','subscription:…')]`, node.log `applied ep6 … applied ep12` then `patch krx-all-2761-ep6 reverted → re-applying`; after unsubscribe `removed ep6 … removed ep12` then `patch krx-all-2761 reverted (restart?) → re-applying`; compose-visitor-b-10-dash-three-loaded-en-1280.png; packages/node/src/market.ts:961-982; packages/web/src/pages/DashboardPage.tsx:246.

items.fix: In `subscribe`, before buying, run the overlap check between the track's bodies and `listApplied()`; refuse (`409 overlaps_loaded {pairs}`) unless `--replace` / `{replace:true}`, printing 'finance/KRX-history would override 241,992 rows of krx-all-2761 (loaded manually)'. Unsubscribe in reverse order inside one runtime lock and re-assert other applied patches afterwards. Show `reason` as a 'Loaded by' column on the dashboard and in `patch stack` (item 216); list the track's items with 1,2,3 badges on the card and in `branch ls`.
items.theme: The runtime stack: apply, remove, watchdog
items.fixed_note: Subscribing reports what the track would write over BEFORE anything is bought and refuses with 409 `overlaps_loaded` unless `--replace` / `{replace:true}`; a body already here is measured exactly, one the subscribe would buy is estimated from the anchors' published address sketches and says so, with no invented row count. The copy says the later one 'wins' (chat.ts:22-29) without saying what winning does to the other knowledge's facts. items.title: With several loaded, the compare shows one answer scored against each knowledge's expectation — two ticks for one text, no way to see which knowledge answered or what the stack changed versus each alone
items.surface: /chat/:ids transcript 'After loading 2/3' bubble (TurnView.tsx:181-216)
items.problem: The node answers once with everything applied and scores that single `patched.content` against every selected anchor's matching sample (market.ts:874-884 `hits[t.id]`), so the bubble renders `pixelplus-087600 ✓ Correct` and `krx-all-2761 ✓ Correct` side by side under one `087600`.
