items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux3/compose-visitor-b-09-turn-two-en-1280.png (After bubble: `1. pixelplus-087600: loaded in 476ms 2. krx-all-2761: loaded in 4.0s`, chips `pixelplus-087600 ✓ Correct  krx-all-2761 ✓ Correct` above one `087600`); compose-visitor-b-09-turn-two.txt; API `benchmark_hits: {pixelplus-087600: true, krx-all-2761: true}` from one `patched` object; packages/node/src/market.ts:874-884.
items.user_cost: The person stacking two or three knowledges is doing it to find out what each adds; the compare cannot tell them. They read two ticks as two independent confirmations, and a ✓/✗ pair as a bug.
items.fix: Caption the hit row 'one answer, checked against each knowledge's expected value' and show both expected values when they differ. Add an opt-in 'Each alone' view for 2-3 selections that runs N+1 patched generations under the same lock (cost N tries, stated up front) and renders columns 'A only / B only / A+B'.
items.theme: Stacking in the live test
items.fixed_note: The hit row is captioned "One answer, checked against each knowledge's own expected value", names each knowledge rather than its id, and prints the per-knowledge expected values whenever they differ — so two ticks no longer read as two confirmations and a correct beside a wrong no longer reads as a bug. The suggested opt-in "Each alone" view was deliberately not built: it spends one free try per knowledge per question and needs a node-side multi-generation lock, and the misreading this finding reports is closed by the caption.

items.title: Load order is tick order and cannot be changed except by unticking and re-ticking — which throws away the conversation and renumbers everything — while three different orderings of the same three knowledges are on screen at once
items.surface: /chat/:ids picker order badges (KnowledgePicker.tsx:107-115), ChatPage.tsx:346 toggle, the head list
items.problem: `toggle()` only appends or removes (ChatPage.tsx:346); there is no move-up/down or drag (`grep reorder/move` → none). Because transcripts and the basket are keyed by the id sequence (`selectionKey = ids.join(',')`, ChatPage.tsx:165/198/242), moving KRX-final from position 1 to 3 changes the key twice and lands on an empty transcript (the transcript loss itself is critique-1 item 14). The picker renders `items` in catalogue order and only decorates ticked rows with a badge (KnowledgePicker.tsx:194, :107-115), while the head list renders `selectedList` in load order: after a re-tick the picker column reads 2 / – / – / 1 and the head reads 1 Pixelplus, 2 KRX final.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux3/compose-visitor-b-01-picker.txt (`order badges: 1,3,2` → untick first → `badges: 2,1`, url `/chat/pixelplus-087600,krx-all-2761-ep12` → re-tick → `badges: 3,2,1`; the winner in every overlap alert flipped); compose-visitor-b-03-untick-first-en-1280.png, compose-visitor-b-04-retick-last-en-1280.png; compose-visitor-b-09-turn-two-en-1280.png (left column badge 2 above badge 1, right head `1 Pixelplus … 2 KRX`).

items.theme: Stacking in the live test
items.fixed_note: Every ticked card carries up/down buttons (and Alt+arrow keys) writing the new order into the address without unticking anything, and ticked cards are listed first in load order under "Loaded, in this order", so the picker column, the head list and the badges finally agree. The transcript survives the change (it is no longer keyed by the selection) and the stack mark says where the order changed.

items.problem: `selectedOverlaps` filters overlaps to pairs where both ids are in `selectedIds` (:89-94), so an overlap between what the visitor ticks and what the operator pinned is never shown although the node has it; `full = selectedIds.length >= MAX_CHAT_PATCHES` (:79) counts only ticks, so with three pinned a visitor can put six on the table; pinned rows are tickable and get an OrderBadge beside the Pinned chip (:109-129). market.ts:839-843 then removes a ticked pinned patch for the Before column, contradicting chat.ts:25 '"Before loading" already includes it'.

items.fixed_note: Pinned ids are position 0 in the overlap computation, so an overlap between what the visitor ticks and what the operator keeps loaded is shown with the pinned side named; the count row says how many more this node keeps loaded; the contamination banner names only the pinned knowledge that is NOT ticked; and a pinned card that IS ticked says "Already in the model — unloaded for the Before loading answer, then put back" instead of "Loads 1.". items.title: The knowledge page's overlap table has three fixed sentences and no idea of lineage: a declared parent is flagged 'Different subject — overlapping entries need reconciling' ten lines below 'Origins', every same-schema row says 'contradictory or a newer version', and there is no 'test both' link
items.surface: Knowledge page › Origins & derivatives › overlap check (PatchPage.tsx:438-486; detail.ts:181-190)
items.problem: `conflicts()` (market.ts:368-388) classifies every overlapping blob by schema equality and `cross_branch` only and never consults parents/children, so a parent sharing 2,992/2,992 addresses appears in the conflict table; `relation()` (PatchPage.tsx:438-443) picks one of three strings (`rel_cross_branch` / `rel_same` / `rel_other`). The note above promises 'Knowledge that does not overlap is safe to load together' and stops; for overlapping rows there is no consequence, and the only chat link on the page is the single-id `/chat/krx-all-2761`. The response already carries `supersedes`/`superseded_by` and `lineage`, so the real relation is computable. (The automatic supersede that branded Pixelplus 'replaced' is critique-2 items 150/151.)
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux3/derive-build-39-child2-origins-en-1280.png ('Origins: pixel-base' and the same id under 'need reconciling'); money-trust-12-15-lineage-text.txt (pixel-deriv-c: parent pixel-deriv-b 'Different subject — overlapping entries need reconciling'); compose-visitor-b-07-detail-overlap.txt / -en-1280.png (`krx-all-2761-ep12 241,992 … Same subject — contradictory or a newer ve… Newer version available`; `links in lineage section: ['/chat/krx-all-2761']`); packages/node/src/market.ts:368-388; packages/web/src/pages/PatchPage.tsx:438-486; packages/web/src/i18n/pages/detail.ts:181-190.
items.user_cost: A visitor deciding whether to compose two knowledges gets a table that says the pair is either contradictory or a version — it does not know which — and the product contradicts itself on one tab.
items.fix: One relation function fed by the detail response: id ∈ `lineage.parents/children` → 'origin / built on this — shares n of m rows'; id ∈ `supersedes` → 'older version — do not load together'; id ∈ `superseded_by` → 'newer version'; otherwise 'overlaps — they answer {n} of the same questions ({d} differently)' from the sample intersection (item 222). Per row add a 'Test both →' link to `/chat/<this>,<other>`. Server side, `conflicts()` skips declared parent pairs (design §12.6).
items.theme: Stacking in the live test
items.fixed_note: relation() is fed by lineage.parents/children, supersedes and superseded_by instead of same_schema/cross_branch alone: krx-all-2761-ep12, drawn as "Origins" ten lines above, reads "Origin — this knowledge was built on it" plus "It is also the version this one replaced"; a plain older version reads "Older version — this one replaces it; do not load both". Where two knowledges genuinely just overlap the row states the consequence (whichever is loaded last wins) instead of guessing at a cause, the note above says the same, and every row carries "Test both →" to /chat/<this>,<other>. `conflicts()` skipping declared parents server-side stays node work.

items.title: The agent loads and unloads knowledge by calling scripts/patch.py directly — outside the node's lock and `applied` table — and by default unloads it again, reverting the shared rows of whatever the node keeps loaded; its default model endpoint is a different server than the node's
items.surface: `ainize-agent run` step [6] (packages/agent/src/agent.ts:252-266); `--api`, `--keep` defaults (bin.ts:39-42)
items.problem: agent.ts:252-266 `execFile`s `python3 scripts/patch.py apply/remove` in `--repo` (default /mnt/newdata/qwen3.8) with no lock, then `remove`s unless `--keep` (default false). The node whose model it is never learns: no `/api/patches/:id/apply` call, nothing in `applied`, nothing in node.log. `--api` defaults to `ENGRAM_API_PUBLIC ?? 'http://localhost:8000'` rather than the runtime the market node reports at `/api/runtime`.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux3/compose-dev-16-overlap-agent-script.txt PART 2 (`[6] loading into the running model (no restart) 끼움: 2992행` … `restored (subscription ended): 뺌: 2992행`; afterwards `/api/runtime applied: [('krx-all-2761','manual')]` and `node.log runtime lines since …: 0`); compose-dev-14-agent.txt (`--api … [default: "http://localhost:8000"]`, `--keep … [default: false]`); packages/agent/src/agent.ts:150, :252-266; packages/agent/src/bin.ts:39-42.
items.user_cost: An agent that 'checks then restores' un-teaches part of the operator's pinned set on every run (item 208's mechanism), competes with the node's own writes, and — with the default `--api` — may measure before/after on a model that is not the one it patched. The developer reading the node's console sees nothing.
items.fix: Give the agent two modes: (a) 'own node' — call `POST /api/patches/:id/buy {apply:true}` on `--node` (the buyer's node does lock, journal and watchdog); (b) 'raw' — only with an explicit `--repo`, taking the same lock dir (`<patchDir>/.ainize-runtime.lock`, runtime.ts:115-160) and defaulting to `--keep`. Read `api` from `GET <market>/api/runtime` when `--api` is absent; refuse to apply when the market's model id differs from `/v1/models`.
items.theme: Agents, the API and routing
items.fixed_note: The agent no longer touches a shared model nobody told: `--repo` has no default, and with one it takes the node's own cross-process lease (<repo>/ple_patch/.ainize-runtime.lock, 15-minute stale break) for the whole apply → ask → restore window, leaves the patch loaded unless `--restore` is passed (the old default removal wrote the model's own rows back over the operator's), and refuses a serving model whose id is not the anchor's; `--api` is read from the market node's GET /api/runtime instead of defaulting to localhost:8000. Verified live: the agent measured against the node's own runtime url and printed the load command instead of writing.

items.title: The agent pays again on every run for a body it already holds — the 402 is always requested and always paid, so a scripted 'ensure these are loaded' loop is a subscription to the seller's price
items.surface: `ainize-agent run` steps [3]-[5]; GET /x402/patch/{id}
items.problem: `runAgent` always GETs the gateway and pays any 402 (agent.ts:193-215); the only memory is 'body already present — download skipped' *after* paying (:231-244). The seller side has no notion of a returning buyer either: `x-ngram-buyer` is sent by market.ts:637 but the gateway route answers 402 to any request without `X-PAYMENT` (api.ts:822-836). Balance 100 → 75 → 50 for two runs of the same command; a cron'd daily agent bought the same bake three mornings running (seller's SOLD 0 → 3).
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux3/compose-dev-05-agent-buy.txt (run 2: `body already present — download skipped` after `settled: tx …`, balance 75 then 50); daily-consumer-20-agent-superseded.txt (run 3: `402 Payment Required … settled` then `body already present`); daily-consumer-25 `patch ls` SOLD 3; packages/agent/src/agent.ts:193-244; packages/node/src/api.ts:822-836.
items.user_cost: An agent cron job composing three knowledges nightly pays three prices per night for bodies it holds.
items.fix: Keep a `purchases.json` in the agent home keyed by `patch_sha256` (manifest + tx) and skip the gateway when the body and a settlement exist, printing `already bought on <date> (tx …)`; add `--repay` to force. Server side: when `x-ngram-buyer` has a settle record for this resource, answer 200 with a fresh manifest instead of 402.
items.theme: Agents, the API and routing
items.fixed_note: The agent writes `<home>/purchases.jsonl` on every settled purchase (knowledge, seller, amount, scheme, tx, gateway, path) and checks it BEFORE touching the gateway, so a cron'd `agent run` no longer pays the seller's price every morning; `--repay` is the deliberate second purchase. Verified by test: the second run of the same command makes no second settlement on the seller's ledger and leaves the balance unchanged, and `--repay` does make one. The server-side half of the reviewer's fix (answering a settled buyer 200 instead of 402) is in the money group's gateway region.

items.title: Asked about Pixelplus, the agent finds the 0.1-CREDIT single-fact knowledge and switches itself to the 25-CREDIT final because of the supersede mark — and `agent catalog` hides the cheaper item, so the developer cannot even see the choice
items.surface: `ainize-agent run` (search mode); `ainize-agent catalog`
items.problem: `pickPatch` follows `superseded_by` whenever no explicit `--patch` is given (`followLatest = true`, agent.ts:112-117, :180) and only checks `--max-price` afterwards (:188). `catalog` defaults to `status=LISTED` (bin.ts:61), which excludes every SUPERSEDED item although the market sells them.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux3/compose-dev-14-agent.txt (`ainize-agent catalog` lists only `krx-all-2761 … 25 CREDIT`; `run --question "Samsung and Pixelplus ticker codes" … --max-price 1` → `pixelplus-087600 is superseded by krx-all-2761 (newer patch on the same benchmark) → switching` → `agent failed: price 25 CREDIT exceeds --max-price 1`); discover-home-21-agent-cli-json.txt; packages/agent/src/agent.ts:112-117, :180-188; packages/agent/src/bin.ts:61.

items.theme: Agents, the API and routing
items.fixed_note: `pickPatch` prints the match with its price, rows and status before choosing, a supersede switch prints `0.1 → 25 CREDIT` with the rows and author, and the switch is refused when the newer version costs more than the item asked for — the agent then buys what was asked for and says why. `agent catalog` defaults to LISTED,SUPERSEDED with the status coloured and a `newer: <id>` note, so the cheaper item is visible at all. Verified by test in both directions.

items.title: `ainize-agent run --patch X` judges X against the Pixelplus demo: `--question`, `--prompt` and `--expect` default to the demo values, so an agent told to buy krx-all-2761 declares FAILED or 'nothing to buy' on 087600
items.surface: `ainize-agent run` defaults (bin.ts:34-38; agent.ts:160-166)
items.problem: bin.ts:34-38 hard-code `--question '픽셀플러스 종목코드 알려줘'`, `--prompt '종목코드 픽셀플러스 '`, `--expect '087600'`; `runAgent` prints `[1] question:` but asks the model `--prompt` and returns 'correct — nothing to buy' when the base already hits. Nothing derives the check from the chosen anchor's benchmark samples, which every LISTED knowledge carries.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux3/compose-dev-04-agent.txt (`run --patch krx-all-2761,pixelplus-087600` → `[1] question: "픽셀플러스 종목코드 알려줘" current answer: "087600…" → correct — nothing to buy`); compose-dev-16 PART 2 (`run --patch pixelplus-087600 --expect 087600` → `answer with knowledge: "36,950 +1" → mismatch … result: FAILED`); packages/agent/src/bin.ts:34-38; packages/agent/src/agent.ts:160-166.

items.theme: Agents, the API and routing
items.fixed_note: `--question`, `--prompt` and `--expect` no longer default to the Pixelplus demo. With `--patch` or `--track` and no prompt, the check comes from that knowledge's own first benchmark sample and the run says which sample it took; the demo fills in only when nothing at all was named, and says so. The step is labelled `prompt:`. Verified by test: a run against a knowledge with its own benchmark measures its sample and never mentions Pixelplus.

items.title: Routing matches on any single key, picks the first tie silently, and returns nodes that once subscribed with no knowledge of which version — if any — they have loaded
items.surface: GET /api/route · `ainize route k=v …` · /network Gateway router
items.problem: `route` scores a branch by the number of equal keys and takes the best with `score > bestScore` (market.ts:993-1006): `market=KRX foo=bar` returns finance/KRX-latest with one of two keys unmatched, `market=KRX` alone returns whichever of KRX-latest/KRX-history comes first. Nodes are filtered by the latest ledger subscribe record only; `selfInfo` (market.ts:1008-1013) carries `branches` and `blobs` but not the applied set, and apply failures inside subscribe are logged as warnings (:975-976), so the subscribe record stands whatever is loaded. Reproduced: `ainize route market=KRX freshness=daily` returned node-c as SERVING NODE while its applied set was the superseded day-1 bake (later, the REJECTED one).
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux3/compose-dev-10-cli-nogpu.txt (`ainize route market=KRX foo=bar` → `→ branch finance/KRX-latest {"market":"KRX","version":"latest"}`); critic-bc-01-livechecks.txt; daily-consumer-23-route.txt; critic-06-route-stale-node.txt (node object has no `applied` key); packages/node/src/market.ts:993-1013.
items.user_cost: An agent that routes by context can be sent to a node serving the wrong track, a stale version, a rejected bake, or nothing at all, and has no field to check before sending traffic; 'freshness=daily' is decoration.
items.fix: Return `{ branch, matched, unmatched, candidates, current_patch_id, nodes: [{…, applied: [ids], current: bool}], stale_nodes }`; require every query key to match unless `?partial=1`; include `applied` in PeerInfo/`selfInfo`; in the CLI print 'matched market=KRX; version not specified — 2 tracks match, showing finance/KRX-latest' and mark stale nodes.
items.theme: Agents, the API and routing
items.fixed_note: Every attribute must match or `/api/route` refuses and names the closest tracks and what they do not answer; `--partial` / `?partial=1` asks anyway. The answer carries matched / unmatched / candidates / ambiguous / current, ties resolve deterministically, and `PeerInfo.applied` (what a node has LOADED) makes every routed node either "serving the whole track" or "missing <ids>", with `stale_nodes` beside them. The CLI and /network render all of it. Verified live: after node-c subscribed without loading, `route market=OVL` printed `missing b-overlapper` and the warning.

items.title: The x402 developer path stops at 'sign a payment intent': the intent hash formula and the signature scheme a third-party client must reproduce exist only in agent.ts and market.ts
items.surface: /docs 'Automatic payment flow (developers)'; OpenAPI `X402Payload`
items.problem: `X402Payload.txHash` is described as 'local-credit: intent hash' and `proof` as 'buyer signature over the intent hash' (openapi.ts:29); /docs step 2 says 'credit mode: sign a payment intent' (docs.ts:31). The actual rule — `sha256Hex(canonicalJson({resource, amount, nonce, payTo, from}))` signed with the buyer key via `signMessage` — exists only at market.ts:549-567 and agent.ts:133; grep of openapi.ts/docs.ts/README for the formula finds nothing user-facing.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux3/compose-dev-12-x402.txt (the 402 body and `x-payment-required` carry scheme/payTo/amount/nonce but nothing about building `X-PAYMENT`); packages/node/src/openapi.ts:29; packages/web/src/i18n/pages/docs.ts:31; packages/node/src/market.ts:549-567; packages/agent/src/agent.ts:133.
items.user_cost: A developer writing a Python or Go agent has to read TypeScript to pay; a wrong field order gives 'payment rejected: 402' with no hint which part of the intent is wrong.
items.fix: Add to `X402Payload` and /docs the exact canonical JSON (key order, no whitespace), the hash, the signature function (ain-util `signMessage`), one worked example with the demo nonce, and a `POST /x402/verify` dry-run that says which field mismatched; ship the ~20-line `payFor` as a snippet in three languages.
items.theme: Agents, the API and routing
items.fixed_note: New /docs page "Paying from your own client" (docs/{en,ko}/reference/x402.md): the canonical intent JSON with its sorted key order, the sha256, the AI Network message hash written out byte for byte, both schemes, and a client that was run end to end against a real node.

items.title: The x402 quote an agent pays against carries no status, no lineage, no licence and no split — a superseded version is quoted like a current one, the royalty map arrives only in a header after the money moved, and the CLI prints the 'newer version' note as a green tick
items.surface: GET /x402/patch/{id} (`requirementsFor`); `ainize use <superseded-id>`; `patch buy` receipt
items.problem: `requirementsFor` (market.ts:525-536) returns scheme/network/asset/payTo/maxAmountRequired/resource/description/nonce/expires_at only — verified live: `curl -i :3402/x402/patch/krx-all-2761-ep12` → 402 with exactly those fields; the royalty map is set in `x-payment-response` after `settlePayment` (api.ts:845), `buy()`'s steps never read it and `patchBuy`'s receipt prints only the steps (patch.ts:196-206). `patchUse` prints the newer-version note through `ok()` — a green ✓ — one line above `✓ bought` (patch.ts:293). (Critique-1 item 4 is the web tab; this is the terminal and the wire.)
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux3/compose-dev-16 PART 1 (`✓ note: a newer version exists on the same subject → krx-all-2761` immediately followed by `✓ bought pixelplus-087600 for 0.1`); compose-dev-12-x402.txt; money-trust-05-x402-quote-derivative.txt; critic-bc-01-livechecks.txt; packages/node/src/market.ts:525-536; packages/node/src/api.ts:845; packages/cli/src/commands/patch.ts:196-206, :293.
items.user_cost: A script assembling a set from ids seen last week silently buys and stacks retired versions; an agent cannot decide on lineage, licence or who is paid before paying, and the buyer never sees the split it just funded.
items.fix: Add `status`, `superseded_by`, `license`, `lineage: {parents, standalone}` and `split_preview` to the 402 JSON body and the manifest; render the note with `warn()` and require `--allow-superseded` (or `[y/N]`) before paying; print the royalty map from `x-payment-response` as a last receipt line (`paid: bob 3.5 · Dana 3.5 · alice 3 (lineage)`).
items.theme: Agents, the API and routing
items.fixed_note: The 402 carries status, superseded_by, license, lineage{parents,standalone} and split_preview (computed by the same royaltyPlan that settles the sale); `use`/`patch buy` render a superseded version as a warning that must be answered with --allow-superseded, and the quote prints the split and the licence before the confirmation.

items.title: `branch subscribe` writes a permanent public ledger record naming your node and the track, and neither the CLI nor the console says so before or after
items.surface: `ainize branch subscribe` → ledger `subscribe` record; GET /api/ledger?kind=subscribe
items.problem: `subscribe` appends `{ node, branch, action, patch_ids, created_at }` to the ledger and broadcasts it (market.ts:964-967); the CLI says only `✓ subscribed`. The `patch_ids` copy is redundant with the branch's own public list, so the disclosure is 'node X subscribes to track Y' — which the router exists to publish — but nothing tells the operator that subscribing is a ledger write while manual `use`/`apply` leaves no trace.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux3/compose-dev-15-subscribe.txt (`curl /api/ledger?kind=subscribe` → `{'node': '0x9103…25e6', 'branch': 'finance/KRX-history', 'action': 'subscribe', 'patch_ids': […]}` readable anonymously on node-a); critic-bc-01-livechecks.txt; packages/node/src/market.ts:964-967.
items.user_cost: An operator who treats tracks as a private convenience has announced their node's role to every peer, forever, without being told.
items.fix: Say it before it happens: `subscribe` prints 'this writes a public record that node-d serves finance/KRX-history' and asks (`--yes` to skip); keep `patch_ids` out of the record so what is published is the routing intent, not the inventory.
items.theme: Agents, the API and routing
items.fixed_note: `branch subscribe` says before it happens that it appends a public record naming this node and the track, readable by every peer for good (unsubscribing appends another record, it does not remove this one), and that loading the same knowledge by hand leaves no trace outside this node; the confirmation is now asked whether or not there is anything to pay, since the disclosure was what was missing. Keeping `patch_ids` out of the subscription record is the node-side half and belongs to the lineage group's subscribe().

flows.name: C. The daily bake
flows.description: Produce fresh knowledge every day from live data and share it through a track that consumers stay current on.

items.title: The dataset door cannot publish from the terminal — every morning's bake ends with 'open the browser'
items.surface: `ainize teach train --wait` / `teach status` end state; POST /api/teach/jobs/:id/publish
items.problem: The CLI drives the whole dataset pipeline (upload → train → wait → READY) but has no `teach publish`: re-run `ainize teach --help` lists status / dataset / train / jobs only, and `renderTeachStatus` ends a READY lesson with `ready: open <node>/teach/lesson/<id> to try it, keep it private or publish it`. Publishing needs `POST /api/teach/jobs/:id/publish` with a `claim_sig` signed by the teaching key (`verifyMessage(ch.claim, body.claim_sig, signer)`, teach.ts:1721) plus both consents (:1720; api.ts:703-712) — the CLI already holds that key in `<home>/teaching-key.json` (`ensureTeacherKey`) and never uses it for this. Only the browser PublishSheet signs the claim (PublishSheet.tsx:63).
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux3/daily-publisher-09-day1-needs-more.txt (end state, no publish hint beyond the URL); critic-bc-01-livechecks.txt (`ainize teach --help`); daily-publisher-s1-lesson-needsmore-en-1280.png (the page the CLI sends you to); packages/node/src/teach.ts:1720-1721; packages/node/src/api.ts:703-712; packages/web/src/components/chat/PublishSheet.tsx:63.
items.user_cost: The cron job stops one step short every day: someone has to open /teach/lesson/<id>, type a name and price, tick two boxes and click Publish at 3 a.m. or at breakfast, so 'bake and share every morning' is not automatable through the door the docs advertise (`ainize teach dataset ./questions.csv --train` is the one-liner on /docs).
items.fix: Add `ainize teach publish <job-id> --name … [--price --license --description --payout <addr>|none] --consent-permanent --consent-rights [--json]`: GET `/api/teach/jobs/:id/publish-challenge` (signed v2 header), sign `claim` with the teaching key via `signMessage`, POST `/publish`, print `published as <patch_id> (ANNOUNCED|PENDING_REVIEW)` and emit `{patch_id, status, url}` under `--json`; exit 3 when the key file is missing, exit 1 on `job_not_ready` with the lesson's status. Add the command to openapi.ts's CLI table and to the READY hint (design §13).
items.theme: The publisher's loop: script, train, verify, publish, supersede
items.fixed_note: `ainize teach publish <job-id> --name … [--price --license --payout --access] --consent-permanent --consent-rights` fetches the challenge, signs the claim with the teaching key the CLI already holds, posts the publish and prints the patch id, the real split, the ledger and the verifier reach; the two consents are never defaulted, and the READY hint and the CLI reference name the command. ADVERSARIAL RE-CHECK: reproduced live — `ainize teach publish <job>` exists, refuses without both consent flags, and publishes with the split and the verifier reach printed.

items.title: `teach train --wait` exits 0 on FAILED and NEEDS_MORE, and prints 'checks passed' over 'taught 0/18'
items.surface: `ainize teach train --wait` exit code and the `checks` line; `job.checks.ok`
items.problem: `waitForJob` returns whatever terminal status arrives (teach-dataset.ts:347-361 TERMINAL includes NEEDS_MORE, FAILED, CANCELLED, EXPIRED, REJECTED) and `teachTrain` just emits it; the `run()` wrapper sets exit 0 (bin.ts:57). The node computes `checks.ok = locality.ok && parent_regression.ok` (teach.ts:1581) while deciding NEEDS_MORE from the taught ratio < 0.75 independently (:1092), so a lesson that taught nothing prints a green `checks  passed` (CLI teach.ts:261) and a JSON `checks.ok: true`. The headline line does say 'NEEDS_MORE — did not stick well enough', so a human is told; a script is not.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux3/daily-publisher-10-known-failed-wait.txt (stream ends `FAILED … error already_known …` followed by `exit=0`); daily-publisher-09-day1-needs-more.txt (`KRX codes 2026-09-01  NEEDS_MORE` … `checks  passed` … `taught  0/18 trained sentences answer right`); the same job's JSON: `status NEEDS_MORE`, `checks.ok True`; packages/cli/src/commands/teach-dataset.ts:347-361; packages/cli/src/bin.ts:57; packages/node/src/teach.ts:1092, :1581.
items.user_cost: A cron line `ainize teach train today.jsonl --wait && ainize teach publish …` proceeds on a failed bake; a script keying on `job.checks.ok` treats a lesson that learned 0 of 18 sentences as a success.
items.fix: In `teachTrain` after `waitForJob` map status → exit code (READY 0; NEEDS_MORE 4; FAILED/CANCELLED/EXPIRED 5; REJECTED 6; timeout 7; READY-unchecked 8) via `process.exitCode` and document them in `--help`. Rename the rendered line to `side-effect check  passed` and add `lesson  did not stick (0/18) — NEEDS_MORE` first when status ≠ READY; in JSON add `ok: status === 'READY' && checks.executed`.
items.theme: The publisher's loop: script, train, verify, publish, supersede
items.fixed_note: `teach train --wait` maps the terminal status to an exit code (0 ready · 4 NEEDS_MORE · 5 failed/cancelled/expired · 6 rejected · 7 timeout · 8 ready-but-unmeasured), --json carries `ok`, and the rendered line no longer prints a green `checks passed` over `taught 0/18`: whether the LESSON stuck is stated first, and `checks.ok` is labelled `side-effect check`. ADVERSARIAL RE-CHECK: the exit table is in EXIT_FOR_STATUS and the READY path exits 0 live. A failing bake could not be produced without an engine, so the non-zero branches stay unexercised.

items.title: A re-bake with identical bytes is accepted as a new knowledge and, once verified, retires the real newer version
items.surface: `ainize publish` / POST /api/patches with a body already on the ledger; `reconcileSupersedes`
items.problem: Publishing the day-1 file again as `krx-codes-2026-09-04` (same sha256 bc8d089c…) created a fresh draft and anchor with no warning — `createDraft` checks only `patch id already exists` (market.ts:308), never `patch_sha256`+author; once verified it superseded day-3 (a genuinely different body) and day-2, because `announce()` records `pending_supersede` from address overlap on the same schema/branch (market.ts:402) and `reconcileSupersedes` writes the records on LISTED (:437-450).
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux3/daily-publisher-22-day4-samebytes-publish.txt (`✓ draft created: krx-codes-2026-09-04 (2,992 rows, sha256 bc8d089c4436…)` = day-1's sha in daily-publisher-03); `patch get` afterwards: krx-codes-2026-09-03 SUPERSEDED sup_by ['krx-codes-2026-09-04'], krx-codes-2026-09-04 LISTED supersedes ['…-09-03','…-09-02']; `ainize logs --kind publish` at 11:51:48; daily-publisher-s2-explore2-ko-360.png (headline card 'KRX codes 2026-09-04 … (nothing changed)', '이전 버전 2개가 숨겨져 있습니다'); packages/node/src/market.ts:308, :402, :437-450.
items.user_cost: On a day when nothing changed, the script publishes the same bytes under a new name; buyers of every previous day see 'Newer version available', the newest real bake is marked retired, subscribers pay again for bytes they already hold, and Explore's headline is the copy labelled '(nothing changed)'.
items.fix: In `Market.createDraft` / `POST /api/patches`: if an anchor by this author with the same `patch_sha256` exists, answer `409 {code:'duplicate_body', existing_id, existing_status}`; the CLI prints `identical to krx-codes-2026-09-01 (published 2026-09-02, SUPERSEDED) — nothing changed; pass --force to publish anyway`. With `--force`, write `parents:[existing]` and skip the supersede of anything newer than `existing`.
items.theme: The publisher's loop: script, train, verify, publish, supersede
items.fixed_note: createDraft refuses `duplicate_body` when a non-DRAFT anchor by this node already carries the same patch_sha256 on the same benchmark schema and branch, naming the existing id, its publish date and its status, with --force to register the bytes again. A forced duplicate cannot retire what came after it either: the supersede cut-off is the date those BYTES first went on the record, not the date of the new anchor. Verified live: the same .npz republished under a new id on the same schema is refused, --force lets it through, and a different schema or branch (deliberately) still coexists. ADVERSARIAL RE-CHECK: reproduced live — re-publishing the author’s own identical bytes is refused with `duplicate_body` naming the existing id and offering --force.

items.title: Today's bake fails verification on any verifier that subscribed to yesterday's — and with two verifiers that leaves it VERIFYING forever
items.surface: Verifier on a node that subscribes to the daily track (verifier.ts:109; market.ts:961-983; catalog.ts:143-157)
items.problem: node-c subscribed to `krx-daily` (day-1 applied persistently). When day-2 was announced, node-c's verifier ran the benchmark with day-1 still in the table: `verify(blob, benchmark, { restore: !m.isApplied(anchor.id) })` (verifier.ts:109) considers only the candidate and `runtime.verify` (runtime.ts:382-421) never removes other applied patches, while the 20-s watchdog keeps re-applying the subscription's day-1 during the run (`patch krx-codes-2026-09-01 reverted (restart?) → re-applying`, node-c 11:46-11:49). Result `pre_apply 3/4`, `free_generation 3/4`, FAIL; node-b passed with RESTARTS 1. quorum = 2, two verifiers, one fail → `quorum_ok` false, failed(1) < quorum(2), attestations > 0 → VERIFYING with 1/2, never LISTED and never REJECTED (catalog.ts:143-157).
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux3/daily-publisher-15-day2-verifying-1fail.txt (`node-c FAIL free_generation=3/4 pre_apply=3/4`, `node-b PASS … RESTARTS 1`); cluster log 11:46:09 / 11:48:09 / 11:49:09; node-a `logs --kind verify`: `node-c verified your knowledge krx-codes-2026-09-02 and it FAILED … {"free_generation":"3/4","pre_apply":"3/4"}`; status still VERIFYING 15 min later; packages/node/src/verifier.ts:109; packages/node/src/runtime.ts:382-421; packages/core/src/catalog.ts:143-157.
items.user_cost: The second morning of the loop produces a knowledge nobody can buy, and the publisher's only signal is `verification 1/2 passed` plus a WARN with a score and no reason. In a small network every consumer node that also verifies breaks the next day's bake for everyone.
items.fix: Before a benchmark run the verifier snapshots and removes the entire applied set (journal in `applied`), runs pre-apply/apply/post, then re-applies the set — and the subscription watchdog must not re-apply while the verifier holds the runtime lock (check `runtime.lockHolder`). Carry `out.details`/`pre_apply` (already logged at verifier.ts:112) into the attestation `score` so the author sees `pre_apply already 3/4 on node-c (had krx-codes-2026-09-01 applied)`. Give VERIFYING an exit: when every known verifier has attested and quorum cannot be reached, derive REJECTED_SPLIT with the counts.
items.theme: The publisher's loop: script, train, verify, publish, supersede
items.fixed_note: Market.verifyIsolated() takes everything that is not the candidate's declared base stack off the table through the journal, runs the benchmark, and puts this node's stack back — so a verifier that also serves a track no longer measures today's bake through yesterday's (AZ-258).

items.title: The publisher's only lever for a stuck day — `patch challenge` — does nothing unless the item is already LISTED
items.surface: `ainize patch challenge` on a VERIFYING item; verifier.ts:52; catalog.ts:148-153
items.problem: Verifiers re-run a challenged anchor only when `e.status === 'CHALLENGED' && e.open_challenge` (verifier.ts:52), and CHALLENGED/`open_challenge` are derived only inside the `quorum_ok` branch (catalog.ts:148-150), so a VERIFYING item with one FAIL cannot be re-verified by anyone: the verifier that failed is blocked by its own earlier attestation (`this node already attested …; a second attestation would not be counted. Re-verification counts after someone challenges …`, verifier.ts:57-63, 91), and the challenge that message recommends is ignored. The CLI still prints `✓ … is off sale until a verifier re-runs the benchmark` (patch.ts:191-192) for an item that was never on sale. (Critique-2 item 153, fixed, covered the LISTED case only.)
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux3/daily-publisher-16-self-challenge.txt (`✓ challenge recorded … ✓ krx-codes-2026-09-02 is off sale until a verifier re-runs …`); `patch get --json` 5+ min later: `status VERIFYING, challenges 1, attestations [node-c False, node-b True]`; no `re-verify (challenged)` line in the cluster log; daily-publisher-s2-logs-day2-en-1280.png vs daily-publisher-s2-day2-challenged-en-1280.png (`Verifying · 1/2`); packages/node/src/verifier.ts:52-63; packages/core/src/catalog.ts:148-150; packages/cli/src/commands/patch.ts:191-192.
items.user_cost: After item 241 the publisher follows the product's own advice, files a challenge, reads a green tick, and waits for a re-run that never comes; the day's bake stays VERIFYING until a third verifier appears.
items.fix: verifier.ts:52: re-run when the newest challenge record is newer than this node's attestation, for any status in ANNOUNCED/VERIFYING/LISTED/CHALLENGED; catalog.ts: set `open_challenge` on non-listed entries too. CLI: when the target is not sellable print `krx-codes-2026-09-02 is VERIFYING (1/2) — asking node-c to re-run` instead of `off sale`.
items.theme: The publisher's loop: script, train, verify, publish, supersede
items.fixed_note: deriveCatalog sets `open_challenge` on entries that were never LISTED and the verifier round answers an open challenge whatever the status is, so a bake stuck at 1/2 with one FAIL can be re-verified; the CLI reports 'VERIFYING (1/2) — the verifiers are asked to run it again' instead of 'off sale' for something that was never on sale. ADVERSARIAL RE-CHECK: reproduced live — a challenge is open whatever the status, the verifiers re-ran it and the challenge_log records dismissed/answered_by; the item returned to sale.

items.title: The operator can `patch announce` a NEEDS_MORE lesson draft straight onto the permanent ledger, skipping the teach gate and the data provider's consent
items.surface: `ainize patch announce <taught-…>` as operator; `market.announce()`; teach.ts:1627
items.problem: A lesson that failed (`taught 0/18`) leaves a private draft `taught-krx-codes-2026-09-01-3da11e` with `visibility: 'test', origin: 'teach', price: '0'` (teach.ts:1627). `market.announce()` (market.ts:390-406) checks only blob presence and `benchmark.schema`, and api.ts:322 routes `/api/patches/:id/announce` straight to it — `origin` is never consulted outside createDraft/updateDraft. So the operator CLI announced it: ANNOUNCED then REJECTED (0/2), hidden from `/api/catalog` by the test visibility but listed on My knowledge as a second row named exactly like the real day-1 knowledge, with no contributor, no consent and price 0. `teach.publish()`'s consent/claim checks (teach.ts:1720-1721) never ran.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux3/daily-publisher-11-announce-needsmore-draft.txt (`✓ announced taught-krx-codes-2026-09-01-3da11e → ledger record 47aa55c6…`); daily-publisher-14-announced-needsmore-get.txt (`price 0 CREDIT`, `verification 0/2`; later REJECTED with node-b 4/10, node-c 6/10); daily-publisher-s2-dash-knowledge2-en-1280.png (row 4: `KRX codes 2026-09-01 · taught-krx-codes-2026-09-01-3da11e · Failed verification`); `/api/catalog?q=taught` → total 0; packages/node/src/teach.ts:1627; packages/node/src/market.ts:390-406; packages/node/src/api.ts:322.
items.user_cost: A publisher scripting `patch announce` on 'the draft the node just made' publishes a stub lesson that teaches nothing, with the visitor's data and no signed claim, onto a ledger that cannot be edited; the dashboard then shows two 'KRX codes 2026-09-01' rows, one 'Failed verification'.
items.fix: In `announce()`: if the draft has `origin === 'teach'` and its job is not PENDING_REVIEW with a verified `claim_sig`, throw `409 lesson_draft: publish it from the lesson page (or \`ainize teach publish\`) so the data provider signs and consents`; never write `visibility: 'test'` anchors from `patch announce` without `--test`.
items.theme: The publisher's loop: script, train, verify, publish, supersede
items.fixed_note: market.announce() refuses a draft with origin 'teach' unless it comes through teach.announceJob(), which is the only path that has checked that the person who taught the lesson published it and that their signed claim verifies; the operator door answers 409 lesson_draft pointing at the lesson page and the Teaching review. Verified live: a draft flipped to origin=teach and announced with `ainize patch announce` was refused with that message and nothing reached the ledger. ADVERSARIAL RE-CHECK: reproduced in packages/node/test/cluster.test.ts — announcing an origin:teach draft through the operator path is refused with `lesson_draft`, and only the teach path (fromTeach) may publish it.

items.title: The bake competes with its own verifiers and consumers for one model lock, and a lock postponement has no deadline
items.surface: Teach worker PREFLIGHT/CHECKING lock retry (teach.ts:1051, :1583-1587); `teach train --wait` stream
items.problem: A model outage has a 15-minute grace (teach.ts:1462-1468), but a busy shared runtime is retried forever: PREFLIGHT `shared runtime busy` → `status: 'QUEUED', blocked: 'lock'` and return (no counter, :1051), CHECKING → `{ retry: 'lock' }` with no `checkWaitSince` (:1587), `exclusive` `waitMs: 2 * 60_000` then requeue. On the throwaway cluster the day-1 check was postponed (`model server busy → check postponed` 11:41:05), the pre-flight bounced QUEUED↔PREFLIGHT twice (`shared runtime busy (pid:2516525: apply)`), and CHECKING of 10 facts took 4 min 33 s while two verifiers and a subscriber apply used the same vLLM. `--wait` prints the same `CHECKING` line throughout (teach-dataset.ts:355 builds it from status+progress only), `teach status` shows `blocked: None`, and the client gives up after 60 min with exit 1 (:358).
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux3/daily-publisher-01-day1-train-json.txt (cut by a 120 s capture timeout during CHECKING); `ainize logs --kind teach`: `11:41:05 model server busy → check postponed`, `11:47:47 model server busy during preflight (shared runtime busy (pid:2516525: apply) — try again later) → requeued`; job queued 11:38:49, finished 11:43:38; `teach status <job>` during the wait: `CHECKING None None`; packages/node/src/teach.ts:1051, :1462-1468, :1583-1587; packages/cli/src/commands/teach-dataset.ts:355-358.
items.user_cost: At 3 a.m. the daily job can sit indefinitely behind verification of its own yesterday's version or a subscriber re-apply, with a terminal that says nothing and a status that says nothing; the script fails on its own timeout with `still CHECKING after 60 min`, not on any node decision.
items.fix: Give lock waits the same bounded grace as outages (`teach.check.lockGraceMs`, default 30 min), after which the lesson is saved READY-unchecked with `checks.note = 'model busy for 30 min'`. Surface `blocked: 'lock'` with the holder (`runtime.lockHolder`) in the job view during CHECKING/PREFLIGHT, print it in the `--wait` stream (`CHECKING · waiting for the shared model (held by node-c: verify) 4 min`), and add `--timeout <min>` with exit code 7.
items.theme: The publisher's loop: script, train, verify, publish, supersede
items.fixed_note: A busy shared model is bounded by `teach.check.lockGraceMs` (30 min) for both the pre-flight and the check, after which the lesson trains on the questions already shown / is saved unchecked; `blocked_by` names the holder, the wait and the grace left, and `teach status` prints it.

items.title: When the model is down at 3 a.m. the CLI goes silent for the whole grace period, and the recovery step exists only in the browser
items.surface: `teach train --wait` on a node whose model server is down (teach.ts:1462-1468); POST /api/teach/jobs/:id/recheck
items.problem: With an unreachable serving API the job trains (stub) and sits in EXPORTED with `blocked: 'runtime'`; the node logs `model server unavailable (serving API unreachable) — waiting before checking` but `--wait` prints nothing after `EXPORTED step 3/3 · 10/10 right` (the stream line omits `job.blocked`). After 15 minutes the lesson is saved unchecked with `publish gated` (teach.ts:1467-1468); measuring it later is `POST /api/teach/jobs/:id/recheck` (api.ts:696), which the CLI does not expose (`ainize teach --help`: no recheck). The READY-unchecked end state is from code, not observed — the throwaway node was torn down at 11:55.

items.theme: The publisher's loop: script, train, verify, publish, supersede
items.fixed_note: `--wait` prints what a lesson is waiting for (`EXPORTED · waiting for the model server (it is off right now)`) instead of going silent for the grace period; `ainize teach recheck <lesson> [--wait]` exposes POST /api/teach/jobs/:id/recheck, which existed only as a browser button; and the exit code 8 for 'READY but never measured' was dead code (EXIT_FOR_STATUS.READY is 0, so the `??` fallback beside it could not be reached) — it is a function now, and the run says publishing stays blocked until `teach recheck` measures the lesson. Verified live against a node whose model server was unreachable: the lesson went READY-unchecked and `teach recheck` re-queued it; a lesson that cannot be re-checked is refused with what to look at.

items.title: Three lessons per key per day, including for the operator's own key on their own node: one failed bake and one retry, and the day is over — with no reset time

items.fix: Exempt the node operator's teaching key (or a `teach.trustedKeys` list) from per-key/IP quotas on its own node; return `{code:'quota_key', resets_at}` (403) and print `daily lesson limit (3) reached — resets 2026-09-03 00:00 UTC`.

items.title: `teach train` on a stub node runs the full live side-effect check on a placeholder — five minutes of the shared model for a lesson that cannot stick
items.surface: `teach train` on stub-backend nodes (node-a :3402, node-u :3422, cluster.mjs default); TeachLessonPage result
items.problem: Every running node reports `backend: stub` with `trainer ready` (`/api/teach/policy` on :3402 and :3422; cluster.mjs:44-49); teach.ts:451 makes the stub skip the live model only when `stubOffline` is set, so on these nodes a placeholder .npz is measured on the shared vLLM for real — ~4.5 minutes — and the lesson ends `NEEDS_MORE · taught 0/18` with a page that says 'Demo run finished — nothing was trained' and still offers `Publish anyway (demo)`. The product does disclose the stub ('backend stub (no GPU training on this node)'); the GPU placement decision is critique-2 item 145. What is new is that the job is accepted and burns the model lock on a placeholder.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux3/daily-publisher-00-nodeu-policy.txt; daily-publisher-09-day1-needs-more.txt; daily-publisher-s1-lesson-needsmore-en-1280.png; node-a log `training started (stub)` 11:39:03 → `NEEDS_MORE: taught 0/18` 11:43:38; packages/node/src/teach.ts:451; scripts/cluster.mjs:44-49.

items.theme: The publisher's loop: script, train, verify, publish, supersede

items.title: Versions are inferred from row overlap, not declared: a bake that touches different rows leaves yesterday listed and selling, a bake with identical rows retires whatever overlaps, and nothing on the web or in `--help` says so
items.surface: `ainize publish` flags; `announce()`/`reconcileSupersedes`; NewPatchPage; the CLI reference
items.problem: Superseding is decided by address overlap on the same schema/branch when the new anchor gets LISTED (market.ts:402, 437-450); grep for 'supersede' in NewPatchPage.tsx and bin.ts finds no declaration flag, and the CLI_REFERENCE publish line (openapi.ts:356) lists `--price --parents --branch --id --test` only. On my cluster the permuted day-3 bake superseded day-2 solely because rows overlapped. A tomorrow whose facts touch different rows (new listings, delistings) leaves yesterday LISTED and both selling; there is no way to keep a point-in-time version listed on purpose or to say 'today replaces yesterday' when rows differ. (Critique-2 item 150 already asks for a `--supersede <id>` confirmation on the retire-your-own-listing path; this is the daily case and the missing intent flag in the web form and docs.)
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux3/daily-publisher-12-day2-publish-plain.txt (two ✓ lines, no conflict info) vs node log `publish: announced krx-codes-2026-09-02 (conflicts: 2)`; `ainize logs --kind publish` 11:51:08 (`krx-codes-2026-09-03 supersedes krx-codes-2026-09-01 (2992 shared rows)`); `ainize publish --help` (no --replaces); packages/node/src/market.ts:402, :437-450; packages/node/src/openapi.ts:356.
items.user_cost: The publisher cannot make 'today replaces yesterday' true on purpose, learns which items got retired only from `logs --kind publish` after verification, and cannot keep a dated snapshot listed.
items.fix: Add `publish --replaces <id>[,<id>]` (and a 'Replaces' picker on /new-patch) that stores `pending_supersede` for exactly those ids, plus `--no-auto-supersede`; at announce print `when verified, this retires: krx-codes-2026-09-01 (2,992 shared rows)` and include `pending_supersedes` in the JSON; document the rule in /docs.
items.theme: The publisher's loop: script, train, verify, publish, supersede
items.fixed_note: `--supersede <id>` now DECLARES a replacement as well as confirming a detected one — the node checks the id is yours, still on sale, older than what you are publishing and not a base this one was built on — so "today replaces yesterday" is true on purpose even when the rows do not overlap. `--keep-others` retires nothing, whatever overlaps. The announce prints what will go, POST /api/patches/:id/announce answers with the same `retires` list, and the rule itself is written out in the daily-publishing guide in EN and KO. Verified live: a declared supersede with 0 shared rows retired the older version, and --keep-others left both LISTED.

items.title: 'Newer version' points one hop up a chain that grows by one every day
items.surface: Knowledge page header 'Newer version:' link; Explore card; `patch get`; catalog.ts:119-123
items.problem: `superseded_by` is populated per supersede record (catalog.ts:122) with no chain resolution; PatchPage.tsx:193/212 and PatchListItem.tsx:166 render `superseded_by[0]`, so day-1 shows `Newer version: krx-codes-2026-09-03` after day-4 superseded day-3 (day-3's own page says newer = day-4). grep of core for latest_version/newest finds nothing.

items.title: The public page reports 100 % and 'Verifying 1/2' for a version one verifier failed and the author challenged
items.surface: PatchPage overview (accuracy bar, header status) vs attestations
items.problem: PatchPage.tsx:126 `scoreOf` filters `a.passed && isExecuted(...)` and takes the last passing attestation's score, so a FAIL attestation never reaches the headline; nothing in PatchPage.tsx or detail.ts renders a 'verifier failed' chip (grep for `!a.passed` finds none). The overview read `Accuracy 100% on all 4 questions checked by verifiers · 0/4 before → 4/4 after`, the header `Verifying · Verified on the real model 1/2`, while the attestations held node-c FAIL (3/4, pre_apply 3/4) and an open challenge existed (visible only on /project/…/logs).
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux3/daily-publisher-s2-day2-challenged-en-1280.png vs daily-publisher-s2-logs-day2-en-1280.png (`FAIL by node-c · accuracy 3/4, 3/4`, `challenged by 0x8564…`); daily-publisher-15-day2-verifying-1fail.txt; packages/web/src/pages/PatchPage.tsx:126.

items.fix: Compute the headline from all executed attestations (`4/4 · 3/4 (2 verifiers, 1 failed)`), add a chip `1 verifier failed · re-verification requested` when `attestations.some(!passed)` or a challenge is newer than the last attestation, and link it to the Verification tab.
items.theme: The publisher's loop: script, train, verify, publish, supersede
items.fixed_note: Executed attestations that did NOT pass now reach the page: a chip in the challenge palette beside the quorum line ("A verifier did not pass it →") and a line under the score bar naming the verifier and its score ("node-c scored the same questions 3/4 and did not pass it — that run is not in the accuracy above"), both opening the Verification tab where the failed questions are already listed. The headline stays the passing run's before/after pair, which a failing run cannot be averaged into. Verified in the browser against a controlled detail response, since no knowledge in the live catalogue currently carries a FAIL.

items.title: Every morning's bake raises a WARN telling the publisher that their own new version retired their own old one
items.surface: market.ts:258-259 author notices; `ainize logs --level warn`
items.problem: `noticeOwnEvents` emits `warn publish: <new> supersedes your knowledge <old> — buyers now see "Newer version available"` for every supersede against the author's own anchors, with no check that `newer` is by the same author on the same branch. Days 3 and 4 produced five such WARNs in ten minutes.

items.theme: The publisher's loop: script, train, verify, publish, supersede
items.fixed_note: `noticeOwnEvents` checks who published the newer anchor: your own replacement on your own branch is `info` and reads like it ("your h-root2-v2 replaces h-root2"), a supersede by anyone else stays `warn` and now names them. Verified on a throwaway cluster with a same-author v2.

items.title: The documented one-liner cannot wait: `--wait` exists on `teach train` but not on `teach dataset --train`

Re-run: `ainize teach dataset upload --help | grep -c -- --wait` → 0, `teach train --help` → 2.

items.title: `--json publish` gives a script nothing to wait on: no record hash, no status, no pending supersedes

items.problem: patch.ts:175 `if (ctx.json) emit(ctx, { anchor: r.anchor, announced }, () => '')` — the ledger record hash returned by `patchAnnounce` (`r.record.hash`, printed only through `ok()` at :181), the derived status, the conflicts computed at announce (market.ts:402) and any verifier count are absent, while the 64-integer `addr_sketch` is included.

items.title: While two verifiers are running the benchmark the consumer sees 'ANNOUNCED 0/2', with no sign that verification is under way or how long it takes
items.surface: `ainize patch ls` / `patch get`; Explore card; catalog.ts:154-157
items.problem: Status becomes VERIFYING only once an attestation exists (catalog.ts:154-155); the 'verifying <id>' line is a local log on the verifier (verifier.ts:63), not a ledger record, so during the minutes both verifiers were executing the benchmark the catalog said ANNOUNCED and the explore card 'Registered · awaiting verification'. items.user_cost: A morning script that waits for LISTED cannot tell 'nobody picked it up' from 'almost done'.
items.fix: Let verifiers write a lightweight `verify_started` event (or include `in_progress: n` from local verifier state on the author node) and show `verifying (2 of 2 verifiers running, ~4 min)` in `patch ls`, the card and the page.
items.theme: The publisher's loop: script, train, verify, publish, supersede
items.fixed_note: `verificationProgress` reports what is still to happen before an item is LISTED: who has not attested, how many of those serve this knowledge's model, and how long verification has actually taken on this node before (the median of what happened, null on a node that has listed nothing). It is on GET /api/patches/:id and on every catalogue row, and `patch get` prints it in the minutes before the stall warning takes over. items.title: 'Subscribe' is a one-time snapshot: nothing ever brings today's bake to a subscribed node, while three product surfaces promise the opposite
items.surface: `ainize branch subscribe`; dashboard track card; GET /api/route; OpenAPI, README and dashboard copy
items.problem: `subscribe()` writes a SubscriptionRecord with the track's `patch_ids` at that moment and buys/applies them once (market.ts:961-983). No code reacts to a later `branch` or `supersede` record: p2p ingest only appends to the ledger (p2p.ts:87-92), `watchdog()` only re-applies patches already in `store.listApplied()` (market.ts:723-735), `reconcileSupersedes()` never touches subscribers, `mySubscriptions()` is read only for status/routing (:985-990), and there is no `branch sync`/`pull`. node-c subscribed on day 1; on day 2 the publisher ran `branch add`, the new bake was LISTED 2/2 and superseded day 1 — node-c stayed on krx-daily-2026-09-01 for the rest of the test with `daily/krx ✓` in `branch ls`, `subscribed · 3 knowledge` on the console card, and `/api/route` listing it as the serving node. The copy promises otherwise: OpenAPI 'Subscribe to a branch (load its knowledge and keep it loaded)' (openapi.ts:288), README:151 'subscription → apply + watchdog', dashboard 'Subscribing makes this node fetch every item of the track' (operator.ts:100).
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux3/daily-consumer-16-after-supersede-cli.txt (`patch ls` 09-02 LISTED / 09-01 SUPERSEDED, `branch ls` daily/krx ✓, `/api/runtime` applied = [09-01 subscription:daily/krx]); daily-consumer-17-dashboard-behind-en-1280.png; daily-consumer-23-route.txt; daily-publisher-20-buyer-subscribe.txt and daily-publisher-s3-buyer-dash-en-1280.png (buyer subscribed at 11:50:31, day-3 added 11:50:35, still serving day-1); packages/node/src/market.ts:961-990, :723-735; packages/node/src/p2p.ts:87-92; packages/node/src/openapi.ts:288; README.md:151; packages/web/src/i18n/pages/operator.ts:100.
items.user_cost: The daily consumer's whole loop — subscribe once, receive every morning — does not exist. They serve yesterday's (retired) data indefinitely while every surface tells them they are subscribed and current, gateways route fresh-data requests to them, and an agent auto-updating from the track has nothing to call.
items.fix: Add `reconcileSubscriptions()` to the 20-s tick (server.ts:183): for each branch in `mySubscriptions()`, diff `branch.patch_ids` filtered to LISTED against applied-with-reason `subscription:<name>`; acquire (when `sellable`) + apply new LISTED items, remove items now SUPERSEDED by another member of the same track, and write an event `subscription: daily/krx updated → krx-daily-2026-09-02 (replaced 09-01)`. Trigger the same pass when a `branch` or `supersede` record arrives over p2p/`refreshLedger`. Expose it as `ainize branch sync <name>` / `POST /api/branches/:name/sync`. Until it ships, change the three strings to 'loads the track's current knowledge now' and print `behind: 09-02 available` in `branch ls`.
items.theme: The consumer's loop: subscribe, receive, stay current
items.fixed_note: reconcileSubscriptions() runs on the 20-second tick and `ainize branch sync` / POST /api/branches/:name/sync do it on demand: a live cluster showed node-b buying a knowledge added to the track minutes earlier with nobody touching it, and the console, OpenAPI and README copy now describes that instead of promising it. ADVERSARIAL RE-CHECK: reproduced live — subscribing to a track bought the item published today and reported it.

items.title: A subscription loads a bake that FAILED verification into the serving model, and loads a bake that has not been verified yet
items.surface: `ainize branch subscribe <track>`; POST /api/branches/:name/subscribe; dashboard Subscribe
items.problem: `market.subscribe()` gates only the purchase on quorum: `if (!this.blobs.has(sha)) { buy() }` then `applyPatch(pid)` for every id in the track's `patch_ids`, whatever its status (market.ts:969-979), and `applyPatch` (:696-707) checks blob presence and runtime only. Any node that verified a bake already holds its body, so the buy — and its quorum check — is skipped. Re-subscribing node-c (verifier+serving) after the 09-03 bake had been REJECTED 0/2 printed `✓ subscribed daily/krx` in 2.2 s and `/api/runtime` showed krx-daily-2026-09-03 applied last — with list-order-last-wins the model answers from the failed bake. Earlier, subscribing while 09-01 was VERIFYING 1/2 applied it the same way (`patches 1 (0 listed)` yet `applied krx-daily-2026-09-01`).
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux3/daily-consumer-29-nodec-resubscribe.txt (`✓ subscribed daily/krx` → applied [09-01 (SUPERSEDED), 09-02, 09-03 (REJECTED)]); daily-consumer-25-day3-rejected-cli.txt (09-03 `REJECTED 0/2`, node-b and node-c FAIL 0/4); daily-consumer-05-subscribe-while-verifying.txt; critic-03-subscribe-rejected-track.txt; packages/node/src/market.ts:696-707, :969-979; packages/core/src/catalog.ts:152-153.
items.user_cost: The one guarantee the daily consumer is buying — 'my model serves today's verified data' — is broken by the exact button meant to provide it. A serving node that also verifies (the default cluster shape) ends the day answering from the bake the network rejected, with a green 'subscribed' tag.
items.fix: In `subscribe()` decide per item from the catalog entry, not from blob presence: apply only when `e.status === 'LISTED'` (or `e.sellable && !e.superseded_by.length`); for VERIFYING/ANNOUNCED/REJECTED/SUPERSEDED push `{id, action:'skipped', reason}` and return the list from the API so the CLI/console can print it (item 260). Add the same guard to `applyPatch()` behind a `force` flag for the explicit operator path.
items.theme: The consumer's loop: subscribe, receive, stay current
items.fixed_note: subscribe() decides per item from the catalogue (LISTED and sellable, not blob presence), returns what it skipped and why, and the CLI/console print it — a REJECTED or VERIFYING bake this node already held can no longer walk into the serving model. ADVERSARIAL RE-CHECK: reproduced live — `branch add` refuses a DRAFT with `not_listed` naming the verification state and offering --force.

items.title: A new subscriber buys and loads every version the track ever carried — retired ones included, stacked on the same rows — and `branch add` accepts a still-unverified day, so a track sells yesterday twice
items.surface: `ainize branch subscribe` / dashboard Subscribe; `ainize branch add`; market.ts:949-980; catalog.ts:157-160
items.problem: `branch add` only appends (`addToBranch`, market.ts:949-959, checks that the entry exists and unions the id — an ANNOUNCED 0/2 bake was accepted with `✓ … added to daily/krx`); superseded members stay in `patch_ids`; `subscribe()` walks all of them (:971) and buys each that is `sellable`, which stays true for SUPERSEDED (catalog.ts:160 `sellable = quorum_ok && status !== 'CHALLENGED'`). A brand-new node-d (100 CREDIT) subscribed when the track held [09-01 SUPERSEDED, 09-02 LISTED, 09-03 REJECTED]: it paid 1 CREDIT for the SUPERSEDED 09-01 and applied it, paid and applied 09-02 on top (2 × 2,992 rows on identical addresses), and skipped 09-03 with a warning visible only in `logs`. In `addToBranch`, when the new patch supersedes an existing member, replace it (keep history in the record's `previous` list); refuse or flag adding an item that is not LISTED.

items.title: Every verification of a new bake wipes yesterday's bake from the serving model; the subscriber flaps 'reverted (restart?)' all morning
items.surface: Serving node that is also a verifier (default cluster shape); `runtime.verify`; `ainize logs`
items.problem: `runtime.verify()` computes `wasApplied` for the candidate npz only, applies it, and unless `restore:false` restores with `patch.py remove` = write base over the candidate's addresses (runtime.ts:382-421), never re-applying other applied patches on the same rows. Because all nodes share one vLLM, node-b's verify also hits node-c's applied rows. node-c logged 12 `patch krx-daily-2026-09-01 reverted (restart?) → re-applying` warnings between 11:43 and 11:53 while the network verified 09-02 and 09-03; each gap serves base-model answers, and the message (market.ts:731, hard-coded '(restart?)') blames a restart that never happened.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux3/daily-consumer-12-yesterday-reverted-log.txt (11:43:47, 11:44:27, 11:45:07, 11:45:27, 11:46:07 around `verifying krx-daily-2026-09-02`); daily-consumer-16 `logs --limit 6`; packages/node/src/runtime.ts:382-421; packages/node/src/market.ts:723-735; packages/node/src/server.ts:183.
items.user_cost: On the morning it matters most — when the new bake is being verified — the consumer's model answers from nothing for repeated 20-s windows, and the only trace is a warning that misdiagnoses itself. (Item 241 is the same collision seen from the verifier's result.)
items.fix: In `runtime.verify()`, before `remove`, collect applied patches overlapping the candidate (`store.listApplied()` ∩ address sets) and re-apply them in order after the restore, inside the same lock (or verify with `restore:false` and re-assert the applied stack — the helper of item 208). Reword the watchdog line to `{id} rows were overwritten (verification of {candidate} on this model) → re-applying` by passing the last runtime operation into the log.
items.theme: The consumer's loop: subscribe, receive, stay current
items.fixed_note: the same isolation as 241 — a verification no longer writes the candidate's `before` over rows a subscription owns — and the watchdog's warning names this node's last runtime operation instead of blaming a restart it never checked.

items.title: The paywall is 'do you already have the file': a verifier subscribes to the whole daily track without paying, while a non-verifier is charged per item
items.surface: `market.subscribe` (market.ts:971-976); `mayDownload` (market.ts:511-522); `ainize wallet`
items.problem: `subscribe()` calls `buy()` only when `!this.blobs.has(sha)`; verifiers fetch and keep every body they verify (`blob: fetched krx-codes-2026-09-01 body … sha ok`; `mayDownload` returns true for any node with the verifier role), so on node-c the subscription applied every bake without any settlement — balance 50 → 50, purchases unchanged, `settle records for krx-daily-*: none` — while node-d, a non-verifier, was charged 1 CREDIT per item. node-a's wallet showed `sales 0` after node-c subscribed; its only sale came from the non-verifier buyer.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux3/money-trust-26-verifier-subscribes-free.txt; critic-03-subscribe-rejected-track.txt (balance 100 → 100, purchases 0, bake applied); critic-04-noded-buy-then-subscribe.txt (1 CREDIT per item); node-c `patch get --json krx-codes-2026-09-01`: `applied True, purchased False, has_body True`; packages/node/src/market.ts:511-522, :971-976.
items.user_cost: Verifier operators — the most likely early consumers of a daily feed — never pay the publisher; the publisher's revenue line for the channel silently excludes them.
items.fix: In `subscribe()` (and `patch apply` of a body acquired as verifier) settle the purchase through the x402 path whenever `!e.owned && !e.purchased`, regardless of blob possession; keep the download step skipped. Show `held as verifier — not licensed for use` in `patch get` (item 173).
items.theme: The consumer's loop: subscribe, receive, stay current
items.fixed_note: `resolveTrack`/`subscribe` decide per item from `hasLicense`, not from blob possession: a `licenseOf` row whose source is `verification` is possession only, so a verifier is quoted and charged for every track item it does not own (and `patch apply` refuses a verification copy in the same words).

items.title: `branch subscribe` prints one green tick for a partial failure, writes the record before trying any item, blocks silently for tens of seconds, and closes with copy describing a deferred apply the code does not perform
items.surface: `ainize branch subscribe` (branch.ts:43-49); POST /api/branches/:name/subscribe (api.ts:351); dashboard Subscribe
items.problem: `subscribe()` appends the subscription record first, then loops with `try { buy } catch { log('warn'); continue }` and `applyPatch().catch(log)` (market.ts:965-978); the route returns `{ok:true}` (api.ts:351); the CLI POSTs with a 30-minute timeout and prints nothing until the node finishes (measured 35.4 s and 14.3 s of silence; node-c's first subscribe exceeded a 120 s capture), then `✓ subscribed krx-daily (patches acquired and applied when a runtime is available)` and exit 0 — even when a member could not be bought (`could not acquire krx-codes-2026-09-02: verification quorum not met — refusing to buy` appears only in the node's log). The closing text implies deferred application, but `subscribe()` checks `st.available` once (:970, :978) and nothing applies later — the watchdog only re-applies already-applied patches. (The no-progress pattern is critique-2 item 105; the swallowed per-item failure and the false copy are new.)
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux3/daily-publisher-20-buyer-subscribe.txt (`✓ subscribed … exit=0`) vs buyer node.log 11:50:32 WARN; daily-consumer-28-noded-subscribe.txt; daily-consumer-05-subscribe-while-verifying.txt (`real 0m35.396s`, exit 0 while 0 listed); daily-publisher-07-nodec-subscribe.txt (empty at 120 s); packages/node/src/market.ts:965-978; packages/node/src/api.ts:351; packages/cli/src/commands/branch.ts:43-49.
items.user_cost: A cron'd `ainize branch subscribe` cannot tell a full success from a morning where nothing was acquired; an operator whose model was restarting when they subscribed believes the track will load itself and it never does.
items.fix: Return `{ ok, items:[{id, status, action:'bought'|'applied'|'skipped'|'failed', reason, amount}] }` from `subscribe()`; the CLI streams per-item steps the way `patch buy` does (quorum, pay, download, waiting for model lock, applied) and exits 1 when any item failed (0 with a warning when items were skipped by status); the console renders the list in a sheet under the card. Either implement deferred apply (`pending_apply:<branch>` picked up by the watchdog) or change the copy to `applied now; nothing is loaded while the model is unavailable`.
items.theme: The consumer's loop: subscribe, receive, stay current
items.fixed_note: `subscribe` quotes the whole track first, buys every `plan: buy` item BEFORE the public record is appended, returns `{acquired, failed, applied, skipped, removed, spent}` per item, and throws 409 `subscription_incomplete` naming each failure rather than printing one green tick.

items.title: Unsubscribe unloads every item of the track, including knowledge the operator bought and loaded on purpose, with no confirmation
items.surface: `ainize branch unsubscribe`; dashboard Unsubscribe (DashboardPage.tsx:249)
items.problem: `subscribe(…,'unsubscribe')` removes every id in the track that is applied regardless of why it was applied (market.ts:981 `for (const pid of b.patch_ids) if (this.isApplied(pid)) await this.removePatch(pid)`), and the console button fires the mutation directly. Reproduced on node-d: `ainize use krx-daily-2026-09-03` (reason 'purchase'), then subscribe, then unsubscribe → applied `[]` and log 'removed krx-daily-2026-09-03'. Note for the fix: subscribe's re-apply overwrote the reason to `subscription:daily/krx` (`store.setApplied` replaces it), so 'only remove reason=subscription' also needs `setApplied` to keep the first reason. (Critique-1 item 9 notes unsubscribe refunds nothing; this is the collateral removal.)
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux3/critic-05-noded-unsubscribe-removes-purchase.txt; daily-consumer-29-nodec-resubscribe.txt (`✓ unsubscribed` → applied `[]`); packages/node/src/market.ts:981; packages/web/src/pages/DashboardPage.tsx:249; packages/node/src/store.ts:508.
items.user_cost: Leaving a track silently reverts a paid, deliberate configuration; the operator discovers it when answers change.
items.fix: Only remove items whose applied reason is `subscription:<name>` (and make `setApplied` keep an existing reason); list what will be unloaded and ask for confirmation in both the CLI (`[y/N]`, `--yes`) and the console; keep purchased items loaded and say so.
items.theme: The consumer's loop: subscribe, receive, stay current
items.fixed_note: Unsubscribe unloads only rows whose applied reason is `subscription:<track>` (in reverse order, cascading), so a knowledge the operator bought and loaded on purpose stays loaded; the log names exactly what was unloaded.

items.title: No 'you are behind' signal for a subscriber: the card counts knowledge, the retired item's page tells other people to update, and the CLI hides that the applied item is retired

items.problem: The track card renders `{n} knowledge · {subs} subscriber(s) · owner {owner}` with no per-item status and no comparison with what this node has loaded. The 09-01 page carries `A newer version exists: krx-daily-2026-09-02. Subscribed nodes should update.` (detail.ts:192-193, PatchPage.tsx:479) — addressed to the subscriber, shown on a page the subscriber has no reason to open. `branch ls` lists ids without status (branch.ts:22-31); `patch ls` shows SUPERSEDED without marking it applied; `patch get` shows `SUPERSEDED applied` on line 1 with the `superseded by:` hint buried under lineage and no command to run.

items.fixed_note: The track card compares the track with this node: how many of its current knowledge are actually loaded on the model (read from the runtime, never inferred from the ledger), which ones are missing when it is behind, and that Sync now is what fetches them — Sync now already applies the newest LISTED and unloads what it supersedes; when the runtime cannot be read the card says so instead of implying everything is current. items.title: A day whose bake failed verification is invisible to subscribers and mis-described to buyers as 'not verified yet'
items.surface: `ainize use <rejected-id>` (patch.ts:292); track card; `branch ls`; /network tracks table
items.problem: When 09-03 was REJECTED (two FAIL 0/4 attestations) nothing changed for subscribers: the card still says `3 knowledge`, no event, no banner (`noticeOwnEvents` logs only to the author). `ainize use krx-daily-2026-09-03` answers `is REJECTED (verification 0/2) — not verified yet` — patch.ts:292 lumps every non-LISTED/SUPERSEDED status into that string — a finished, failed verification presented as pending. The page header shows 'Failed verification' (good) but the track table on /network and `branch ls` list the failed id as a member with no status.

Track card and `branch ls`: per-item status chips and `latest bake (09-03) failed verification · serving 09-02`. Emit a node event `track daily/krx: 09-03 rejected` for subscribers.
items.theme: The consumer's loop: subscribe, receive, stay current
items.fixed_note: `ainize use` branches on the status: a REJECTED knowledge is reported as a finished, failed verification with the FAIL count and exit 6 (the code `teach train --wait` uses for REJECTED) so a script stops retrying, a RETIRED one as a publisher's withdrawal, and only VERIFYING/ANNOUNCED keep 'not verified yet'. `branch ls` gives every track member its own state (failed verification / challenged / withdrawn / older version / N of M verified) and a track whose newest bake failed says so on its own line with what subscribers keep serving. items.title: A track is an append-only list: unverified and rejected bakes are added and shown to every consumer and gateway, and nothing can ever be removed from a track
items.surface: `ainize branch add`; /network tracks table; GET /api/branches; GET /api/route
items.problem: `addToBranch()` only checks the entry exists and unions the id (market.ts:949-959); there is no remove/retire endpoint, no `branch rm` (bin.ts:383-393 has ls/create/add/subscribe/unsubscribe), and BranchInfo has no per-item status (types.ts:185-193). The publisher's cron adds each bake before verification; after three days the public track shows `krx-daily-2026-09-01, 09-02, 09-03` with one current item, and `/api/route` hands the whole list — REJECTED, SUPERSEDED, LISTED — to gateways.

items.user_cost: Consumers and agents reading the track see three equal ids where one is retired and one failed; the publisher cannot clean it up.
items.fix: Add `POST /api/branches/:name/patches/:id/remove` (owner only) writing a new branch record, `ainize branch rm <name> <id>`, and derive `items:[{id,status,superseded_by}]` in `GET /api/branches` so the CLI table, network table and route response can show status and let clients pick the current item.
items.theme: The consumer's loop: subscribe, receive, stay current
items.fixed_note: `ainize branch rm <track> <id>` takes a knowledge off a track by writing a new track record without it — a track record belongs to the address that first wrote the name, so this is the owner rewriting their own list — after saying how many subscribers stop loading it. Members are shown with their per-item status in `branch ls`. Verified live end to end on a two-member track. Deriving `items:[{id,status,superseded_by}]` inside GET /api/branches so /api/route and the Network table can filter server-side is the lineage group's region and is still open.

items.title: The buyer agent has no way to say 'the daily/krx track, newest verified': no `--track`, no `--watch`, and `--follow-latest` is off whenever an id is given, so a scripted agent keeps buying yesterday's retired bake

items.problem: The run options have no `--track`/`--branch`/`--watch`; `pickPatch(items, …, o.patch ? !!o.followLatest : true)` (agent.ts:180) turns `followLatest` off whenever an explicit `--patch` is given, so yesterday's script keeps buying the retired 09-01 with only a note ('use --follow-latest'); nothing reads `/api/branches` to pick a track's newest LISTED member. items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux3/daily-consumer-20-agent-superseded.txt (run 1: `note: … newer version … use --follow-latest` then paid for 09-01; `run --help` matches only `--follow-latest`); packages/agent/src/bin.ts:33-47; packages/agent/src/agent.ts:112-127, :180.

items.fixed_note: `--track <name>` picks the newest verified, still-current member of a track (a member retired by another member is history, as a subscribing node resolves it), `--follow-latest` now defaults to ON so yesterday's script stops buying the retired bake, and `--follow-price same-price|any` bounds the switch. `watch --track … --interval` is the loop. items.title: The public track list on the demo marketplace is 32 throwaway test tracks that can never be deleted, and the public catalog leaks a hidden test anchor as a child that every other surface hides
