items.problem: node-a `/api/branches` today: 35 branches — 32 `e2e/*` ('O14 test branch'), finance/KRX-latest, finance/KRX-history, an empty `ops/refresh-check-1788174110` — all 0 subscribers. BranchInfo has no `visibility`/`archived` field (types.ts:185-193) unlike `PatchAnchor.visibility` (:106); `branches()` is last-write-wins on name with no delete (market.ts:934-939); the router picks the test tracks up (`jurisdiction=KR-…`). Separately, `curl :3402/api/catalog` shows krx-all-2761 `children ['qa-royalty-child']` while `/api/patches/krx-all-2761` `lineage.children = []` — `relativeVisible` (api.ts:173-177) is applied only to the detail route; the agent catalog (agent/src/bin.ts:64) prints id/status/rows/price/attest/name with no version or lineage columns.

items.user_cost: The one page that is supposed to sell 'subscribe to a track' reads as a test log; a real daily track is one row among dozens of junk rows; and a JSON consumer sees a child the product hides everywhere else.
items.fix: Add `visibility?: 'public'|'test'` and `archived?: boolean` to BranchInfo (owner-only update via a new branch record); hide test/archived tracks from /network, `/api/branches` (unless `include_test`) and `route()`; make the e2e suite create tracks with visibility test. Apply `relativeVisible` to `children` in `/api/catalog` as well.
items.theme: The consumer's loop: subscribe, receive, stay current
items.fixed_note: BranchInfo gained `visibility: 'public'|'test'` and `archived`, owner-only and carried through every update; `GET /api/branches`, `branch ls` and `route()` hide both by default (`?include_test=1` / `--all` still show them). `ainize branch create --test` and `branch archive|unarchive <name>` are the two doors — the record and the subscribers stay, the shelf changes. `/api/catalog` runs `children` through the same `relativeVisible` as the detail route, so a hidden test anchor is no longer leaked as a child. The node half of this landed inside fa2ab45, a concurrent workflow's commit that staged market.ts and api.ts while the change was in the tree. Verified live on all four points.

praise.title: The purchase path is the best-designed step in all three flows.
praise.body: `ainize patch buy` prints a millisecond-stamped timeline (quorum → 402 quote → pay → settled → download), verifies the sha256 against the on-ledger anchor, reuses a body the node already holds instead of downloading 300 MB again, and prints the file path and the next command (derive-obtain-07, compose-visitor-b-08, money-trust-06). The agent's transcript is the same design for a machine: the 402 decoded in plain words, the manifest hash checked against `x-content-sha256`, the body hash checked against the anchor with the sentence 'integrity holds no matter which peer served it', `--max-price` refusing before paying, and a challenged knowledge refused with the verifier's reason (compose-dev-05, agent.ts:185-248). Every fix in this review that touches buying should keep this shape.

praise.title: Money is recorded verifiably, and the settle record is the right primitive.
praise.body: Each settlement carries the full per-address royalty map on the ledger; `royaltySplit` walks parents with a visited set, clamps shares and never exceeds the price; the teacher's public page reads 'owed 0.98 · paid' straight from that record (derive-build-38; catalog.ts:233-291). Items 191–198 are about the rule and its display, not about the ledger — the record is exactly what an auditor needs once the split is written into the anchor.

praise.title: Supersession works end to end and the marketplace hides the noise.
praise.body: On a local ledger, 20 s after day-2 was LISTED, day-1 was marked superseded network-wide; /explore's 'Current only' showed exactly one bake with '1 older version hidden · show' in both languages; /project/<id>/logs shows the whole day as a public timeline — registered, each verifier's PASS/FAIL with scores, the challenge, every 'replaces' record with hashes (daily-publisher-s2-logs-day2, daily-consumer explore captures). A 30-day feed will not bury the catalogue; it only needs the intent flag and the chain resolution asked for in items 248–249.

praise.title: The node refuses to spend money or GPU on the wrong thing, loudly.
praise.body: The teach worker rejects a dataset the model already knows before training ('already_known'); every purchase path refuses a rejected bake with the count that explains why (`REJECTED (verification 0/2)`, 'verification quorum not met — refusing to buy'); `patch forget` refuses when a body is shared by other ids and prints the ALSO STOPS SERVING table with a `--all-sharing` opt-in (patch.ts:283-306); the watchdog notices a reverted table within 20 s and logs the id. Item 208's fix is that pattern — detect shared state, name the collateral, require a flag — applied to `remove`, `subscribe` and `unsubscribe`.

praise.title: Load order is a first-class, honest fact in the live test, and the CLI is the most honest surface about lineage.
praise.body: Numbered badges, 'Loads n.' on each card, a numbered head list, per-knowledge 'loaded in 476 ms / 4.0 s' lines, an order that survives in the URL and a reload; one stacked compare costs exactly one free try and the footer says so (api.ts:405-417). `POST /api/chat` is the one place composition is specified — 'loaded in list order; the last one wins on overlapping memory entries' — and reported per knowledge. `teach status` prints 'taught with pixel-base, pixel-sa (builds on them)', `patch get` shows each parent with its status and the address-set overlap table, and a child published from a stranger's node appeared under the parent's `children` on node-a within seconds of the p2p push (derive-build-23, -44, -51). RUN-LOCALLY.md even states the dependency the Buy tab is missing: 'This lesson was taught with … loaded; load them first for the same behaviour' (teach-recipe.ts:102-103).

praise.title: The raw material for a scriptable daily loop is already there.
praise.body: `teach train --wait` streams stage changes to stderr and keeps stdout clean for `--json`; `patch get --json` is complete enough to script against (status, attestations with scores, superseded_by/supersedes, sellable, quorum_ok); `ainize teach dataset get <id> -o questions.jsonl` exports exactly the rows a lesson was trained on and verifies the fingerprint so re-uploading lands on the same dataset; `login --password`, distinct exit codes and the private-cluster script (`NGRAM_CLUSTER_HOME=… NGRAM_LEDGER=local scripts/cluster-restart.sh`, seeding and verifying the real krx blobs on the real model in about two minutes) made this whole review scriptable without touching the shared chain. The operator's Teaching tab tells the truth about failed bakes in one glance ('Needs more · taught 0/18 · side effects 10/10'). Items 238–239 and 252–253 close the four gaps that keep a cron job from using all of this.

order_of_work:
The two earlier reviews proposed waves A–F (stop the lying, stop the destroying, make the trust claims true, the publisher's dead ends, day-2 operability, polish) and the lineage spec proposes PRs L0–L9. The waves below slot between them: G is the first half of L2 and must precede everything else in this review; J is L0 + L4 with L3 behind a flag; K is L0's money fixes plus two items the spec does not have; I has no counterpart in the spec and is the cheapest large win.

**Wave G — stop the runtime from un-teaching (one to two weeks; the helper is one function).** Items 208, 210, 211, 209, 213, 214, 258, 241, 212, 215. One locked helper — 'after this write, re-apply every applied patch whose address set overlaps, in stored order' — called from `removePatch`, `runtime.verify`, `unsubscribe` and the chat `finally`; a `position` column; the watchdog inside the lock, reading a fresh list; `wasApplied` from the store, not the sample; a `removing` set. This is design L2 without the journal, and until it lands every other fix in flow B and half of flow C is cosmetic. It pairs with critique-2's wave E (the applied-set marker, item 126).

**Wave H — make the daily loop scriptable (one week, all S/M).** Items 238, 239, 240, 242, 243, 245, 252, 253, 246, 244, 247, 251. `teach publish` and `teach recheck` in the CLI; an exit-code table; a duplicate-body check; challenge re-runs on VERIFYING; `announce` refusing lesson drafts; `--wait` on the one-liner; a bounded lock grace with the holder printed; the stub refusing to hold the model. Nothing here needs the GPU decision (critique-2 item 145) to be made first.

**Wave I — make subscribe a channel (two weeks, M).** Items 255, 256, 257, 260, 261, 262, 263, 264, 265, 266, 259, 249, 250, 267, 268, 269. `reconcileSubscriptions()` on the watchdog tick and on incoming branch/supersede records; per-item status gating and results; the resolved current set; `branch rm` and per-item status in the track; `latest_version`; the `as_of` field; a track page; the copy rewrite. This wave makes flow C exist; the spec has no PR for it and should gain one (it sits naturally before L8's bundle).

**Wave J — make "built on" true, or stop saying it (three to four weeks; L0 + L4 first, L3 behind the `teach.lineage` flag).** Items 176, 177, 178, 180, 181, 182, 183, 185, 186, 187, 188, 189, 179, 171, 175, 184. In order: the copy change ('credits', not 'built on') and the silent-drop errors (`parent_not_listed`, `base_rejected`, `unknown parent` with a remedy, `conflicts()` skipping declared parents) — that is L0 and is a few days; then the base row / Start-from block / `--on` (L4); then CHECKING in deployment order and per-source verification; then the trainer on top (L3, GPU time). Wave D of critique-2 (retire, supersede consent, ownership check) should merge into this one.

**Wave K — money you can check (one to two weeks, M).** Items 191, 192, 193, 194, 195, 196, 197, 198, 236, 231. The share written into the anchor and validated on ingest; the chain rule decided and tested; `royalty_preview` on the detail and on the 402; net revenue; a lineage event and per-source royalty attribution; the royalty map on the settle row. This is critique-2's wave C (make the trust claims true) continued into lineage, and it is where an AIN-ledger deployment becomes safe.

**Wave L — see the set (two weeks, mostly S).** Items 216, 217, 218, 219, 220, 221, 222, 223, 224, 225, 226, 227, 228, 229, 230, 232, 233, 234, 235, 237. `patch stack` / `GET /api/runtime/stack` and the console's 'In the model now' table; variadic ids; JSON on mutating verbs; the composition paragraph in the docs; question-level overlap and the per-row relation; reorder controls; pinned items in the cap and the alerts; the agent's own-node mode, budget rule and sample-derived check; route with `applied`; the x402 formula and quote fields. Most of this is display over data the node already computes.

**Wave M — discovery, dead ends and docs (one to two weeks, S).** Items 170, 172, 173, 174, 199, 200, 201, 202, 203, 204, 205, 206, 207, 190, 248, 254. The ledger-mismatch line; the Training-set line and `patch fork`; verifier-held vs bought; the post-purchase actions; live-test misses with prompt keys; `Build on this` and the signals; the three docs sections; the tree, glossary, mobile tabs, search and header fixes. It fits alongside critique-1's own discovery items and can run in parallel with everything above.
